EventNotes:
Welcome to Cross Camp - four nights of cyclocross racing at the iconic Driveway in Austin, TX.

The rules are simple:

  1. Don’t be a jerk.
  2. Abide by all USAC cyclocross rules.
  3. The promoter’s ruling is final.
  4. Gravel and mountain bikes without bar ends are allowed. No maximum tire widths enforced.
  5. Please inform the finish line judges if you withdraw from the race.
  6. Prizes will be awarded 3 deep in competitive categories.
  7. Please patronize our sponsors.
  8. You must check in with the registration staff to be counted in the results.
  9. Absolutely no alochol is permitted on the grounds of The Driveway at any time. 


Entry Fees

Entry fees are $45 for your first race and includes any additional races on the same day (ex. Novice riders may also enter the 3/4 /Novice field on the same day at no additional cost).  Note: You must register for these at the same time to take advantage of this discount.

Season passes are available and will automatically enroll you for 4 nights of the category of your choosing. You may also select additional races throughout the series during your registration if you would like to race multiple categories on some (or all) nights.

Late registration is available this year. Entries after 12 pm the day of each race will incur a $5 late fee and may not be included in call ups. Registration closes 15 minutes before each race wave, so we highly encourage you to sign up as soon as you can!

Racing Licenses

All categories require a USA Cycling license to participate. If you do not have a current USAC annual license you can purchase one at memberships.usacycling.org. 

Course

You will race on +/- 1.5 mile courses taking in new trails connected by fast pavement for a course that's always changing.

 

Parking and directions

Ample parking is available at the Driveway, but we highly encourage you to ride to the races. Please drive slowly on Delwau Ln, respect the venue, their neighbors and be cognizant of bicycles and pedestrians.

Weather

The event is rain or shine. Delays or cancellations may be issued at the discretion of the promoter or race officials in the event of severe weather.

Producers

This event is produced by Camp of Lamps LLC and Holland Racing LLC.

Adventure Cycling Association is celebrating 50 years of bicycle travel in 2026. To mark this milestone, we invite you to join the 50TH ANNIVERSARY DROP-IN RIDES, a celebration across three legendary routes.

WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF THE DROP-IN RIDES?
Drop-In Rides are part of Adventure Cycling’s 50th Anniversary. Just as Bikecentennial ’76 sparked a movement 50 years ago, these rides celebrate where we started, what we’ve accomplished, and where we’re going—inviting riders everywhere to share in the adventure.

THE ROUTES
TRANSAMERICA TRAIL – The original Bikecentennial ’76 route that launched Adventure Cycling. Nearly 4,200 miles from Oregon to Virginia, it passes through small towns, farmland, the Rockies, and Appalachians. Dropping in here connects you with the history of cross-country cycling.

GREAT DIVIDE MOUNTAIN BIKE ROUTE – Since 1998, the world’s premier off-pavement route. Over 2,700 miles of gravel, dirt, and rugged mountain passes from Montana to New Mexico. A true test of endurance and adventure, inspiring riders worldwide.

GOLDEN GRAVEL TRAIL – Created for our 50th Anniversary, debuting in 2026. A mixed-surface journey across plains, canyons, and mountains, designed to showcase America’s growing gravel culture and the future of bicycle travel.

WHERE CAN I LEARN MORE ABOUT THE ROUTES?
Visit our route overview pages to see descriptions, maps, and details to help you choose the ride that fits your goals:

  • Great Divide Mountain Bike Route overview
  • TransAmerica Trail overview
  • Golden Gravel Trail overview (launching early 2026)

HOW DO I GET MY ROUTE AND NAVIGATE IT?
Adventure Cycling offers both paper maps and digital maps for purchase:

  • TransAmerica Trail Maps
  • Great Divide Maps

These maps include turn-by-turn directions, service listings, and detailed navigation notes. Once downloaded, digital maps can be used offline on your GPS device or phone.

Golden Gravel Trail Maps – This brand-new 50th Anniversary route will be free to download starting early 2026.

For more information about digital maps, visit our Digital Routes FAQ.

HOW CAN I FIND A GROUP TO RIDE WITH?
Check out our Companions Wanted listings to connect with others planning to ride.

Adventure Cycling members can post on Companions Wanted (become a member, just $2.50/month), while anyone can respond to a post. Drop-In Rides have a dedicated section in Companions Wanted in celebration of our 50th Anniversary.

EventName: 2026 I Love Gravel Racing Points Series
EventNotes:
2026 I Love Gravel Racing Points Series

Everyone, Everywhere, Every distance

3 distance categories

Short = 24 miles or less, Mid = 25-49 miles, Long = 50+ miles

 

A different approach to a Points Series. There will be 2 categories, Male and Female, no age group, NO E-BIKES. Must be a GRAVEL RACE. No minimum or maximum number of races. No specific races, but Premier Races benefit the participant with double points.

For 2026 we have added Clydesdale and Athena categories. In addition, we will have the Fat Tire and Junior categories that were added in 2025. These categories will have a registration fee of $20 and do not include the opportunity to win FREE, or discounted, race entries. It does include your opportunity to win trophies, swag bags and your private invitation to the Champions Celebration. All details for these new categories are listed below.

Our goal is to increase participation in gravel racing. We are not looking for the fastest Champion. We would like our Champions to be passionate, and engaged, in the gravel racing community. With that thought in mind, the person who participates at more races stands a greater chance of being Champion.

Series will run from March 1, 2026 and end on November 1, 2026. You may sign up for the Series at any point throughout the year, but your points will not count until AFTER you have signed up. No retro results.

**Race results reporting are the responsibility of the participant. Participant must report their results to ILGR through an email (ILoveGravelRacing@aol.com) with a verifiable source, such as timing service or results documentation. Results must be reported within 2 weeks of race completion AND by November 1, 2026.**

$25 fee for registration will include your chance at the Championship. You are not locked into one distance. Your registration will allow you to compete in EVERY distance. 

Points will be awarded for your Overall Male or Female finish at ANY GRAVEL RACE, ANYWHERE. However, we have a group of Premier Gravel Races where double points may be earned. Since we have membership internationally, you may race anywhere, at any distance and participate in this Series.

2026 Premier Races are:

3/28/26 Melting Mann in Jones, Michigan

 4/25/26 Waterloo G & G in Grass Lake, Michigan

5/2/26 Black Fork Gravel Grinder in Glenmont, Ohio

5/23/26 Roughneck Gravel Roubaix in Titusville, Pennsylvania

 6/20/26 Dirty Donut in Martin, Michigan 

7/11/26 Cedar Blitz in Cedar Springs, Michigan

 8/8/26 Frankenmuth Fondo in Frankenmuth, Michigan

 8/15/26 Fast Fitty in Charlotte, Michigan

8/29/26 Thunder Bay Thriller in Alpena, Michigan

9/13/26 Uncle John's Dirty Ride in St. Johns, Michigan

9/19/26 The Dirty Mitten Gravel Race in Middleville, Michigan

10/4/26 Rode to Hell in Chelsea, Michigan

10/24/26 Lowell Classic Fall Gravel in Lowell, Michigan

Points rundown: 1st Overall = 500 points, 2nd = 495, and so on. 101 place Overall through infinity will receive 5 points for completing ANY gravel race. 50 points are earned if someone signs up for the Points Series and you are listed as their referral. 10 points are earned for every race that you start and list ILGR as your team. More referrals, more points. More listings of ILGR as your team, more points.

Awards:  1st Male and Female in each distance will receive a custom Champion jersey, awesome trophy and 11 FREE entries to Premier Races in 2027.

2nd Male and Female in each distance will receive an award and 50% off entry to 11 Premier Races in 2027.

3rd Male and Female in each distance will receive an award and 25% off entry to 11 Premier Races in 2027.

All winners will receive incredible swag bags.

EVERYONE who registers for the Points Series is entered in drawings with more prizes throughout the 2026 race season!!

Junior Category will be a Trophy category. The Top 3 places will receive awards, swag and an invite to the Champions Celebration. This will be a Coed division covering 12 years old and under. One distance category of 24 miles or less. The same point standard will apply. Premier races will be worth double points. Your points will be determined by Overall Junior placement. In the event of a tie, your Premier Race points will be the determination. This category is a separate registration fee from the standard Points Series.  You may enter both. 
 
Fat Tire Category will be a Trophy category, like the Junior Category. It will be a Coed division that will encompass ANY age. Any distance between 1-49 miles will be the category. Top 3 will receive awards, swag and an invitation to the Champions Celebration. The same point standard will apply.  Premier races will be worth double points. There must be a Fat Tire Category for your points to be awarded in this category. Your points will be determined by Overall Fat Tire placement. In the event of a tie, your Premier Race points will be the determination. This category is a separate registration fee from the standard Points Series. You may enter both.
 
Clydesdale and Athena Categories will be a Trophy category. Clydesdale definition for ILGR Points Series is Male weighing 220 lbs. or more. Athena definition for ILGR Points Series is Female weighing 165 lbs. or more.  It will encompass ANY age. Any distance between 1-49 miles will be the category. Top 3 will receive awards, swag and an invitation to the Champions Celebration. The same point standard will apply.  Premier races will be worth double points. There must be a Clydesdale/Athena Category for your points to be awarded in this category. Your points will be determined by Overall Clydesdale/Athena placement. In the event of a tie, your Premier Race points will be the determination. This category is a separate registration fee from the standard Points Series. You may enter both.
 
To allow more people to enjoy our Champions Celebration, we will offer the opportunity for you to purchase tickets to attend. This process allows EVERYONE who wants to share in these special moments to be included.

EventName: 2026 Big Bear Lake Trail Center (WV) Merchandise
EventNotes:
The Big Bear Lake Trail Center is quickly becoming known as the hot spot for classic east coast single track. Years of trail development, by experienced mountain bikers have created a trail system that will have you grinning ear to ear. The terrain has everything to offer; gradual climbs, large embedded rocks, tight slaloms, challenging rock gardens, and off the saddle downhills. Almost 50 miles of trail wind through knee deep ferns, soft needle pine plantations, and groves of mountain laurel. Riders of all ages and abilities will find trails to fit their individual riding skills and need for adrenaline. The Big Bear Lake Trail Center is the place to bring the entire family to experience mountain biking at its best.

We make it easy to find your way around. Trail maps will be mailed to online season pass purchasers or you can ask for one at the main entrance.  We also suggest checking out the TrailForks app or the MTB Project app on your mobile device. Trail fees are $10/day or $30 for a season pass. Season passes will be mailed to you. If you choose to buy a day pass - bring proof of purchase in the form of a printed confirmation email or a screenshot on your phone. A staff member will verify that your pass is valid for that day.

All trails may be used for hiking, trail running, and x-c skiing. Trails are closed from November 1 thtough December 31. Trails are open from January 1 to October 31 each year.

Visit our WEBSITE.

Check us out on FB HERE or our events page HERE.

Cyclists enjoying trails at The Big Bear Lake Trail Center may inquire about overnight camping sites in Beaver Creek Village.

We do not close the trails due to wet conditions.

  4. Season pass $30.00 (BEST VALUE!)

  7. Camping available at Beaver Creek Village sites. Inquire at Guard House or Office or online HERE.
  8. Helmets and personal safety equipment required.

The series takes place in the Quad Cities which is located on the Iowa Illinois border, nestled between the Mississippi River and Rock River. 

The series consists of four events

Hell of the Wind- March 28th, New Liberty, IA

1904- April 25th, Morrison, IL

Burning Quad- July 11th, Erie, IL

Turkey Burner- October 31st, New Liberty, IA

For detailed information on each event, check out their respective Bike Reg page or our website bigrivergravel.com for further details. 

Gravel Riding Series Competition-

For the first time ever, the Big River Gravel Series will have an overall series payout for the top 3 men and women in the Mississippi distance. In order to be eligible for the payout a rider must sign up for the entire series using the Big River Gravel Series registration page. It is a dynamic payout. If 50 or less riders register for the Mississippi distance series the payout will be $500. For every rider who registers for the Mississippi distance once over 50 riders, the payout increases by $50 per rider registered. Example- 100 total riders register for the Mississippi distance series, the payout would be $3,000. 

Riders must decide if they want to compete in the Mississippi River (long distance) or the Rock River (short distance) for the series and stick with that distance for the entire series. If a rider switches distances, their points will start not carry over to the new distance series competition. 

The Big River Gravel Series will have an overall series payout for the top 3 men and women in the Mississippi distance. In order to be eligible for the payout a rider must sign up for the entire series using the Big River Gravel Series registration page on BikeReg. The rider must also finish all 4 events.

There will be a series competition for overall (women/men) in each distance, age group (women/men), and a single speed open. Riders are eligible for both point series competitions. 
 
There will be a podium for top three overall (women/men) in each distance and top three in each age group (women/men). Riders are eligible for both the overall and age group podium.

Age group categories are divided as follows. There will be an age group category for women and men. 19 and under juniors, 20-44, and 45+. 
 
Scoring for the overall and age group categories will work as follows. 1st= 10 points, 2nd= 9 points, 3rd= 8 points, 4th= 7 points, 5th= 6 points, 6th= 5 points, 7th= 4 points, 8th= 3 points, 9th= 2 points, 10th= 1 point

Scoring for the series will be based on a riders accumulative points from all 4 events.

BIRDEYE ULTRA

UNSUPPORTED. UNREASONABLE. UNFORGETTABLE.

 

 

THE CHALLENGE

Two routes. One starting line. Birdeye.

BIRDEYE 500

Ride the entire Crowley’s Ridge Gravel Trail—twice.

An enormous self-supported journey through the Arkansas Delta, connecting rural communities, state parks, gravel roads, and the full length of Crowley’s Ridge.

NIGHT OWL 200

Ride from Birdeye to Helena and back.

A long beautiful ride through the Delta for those looking to push themselves without committing to the full 500.

 

THE RULES ARE SIMPLE.

Ride the route.

That's it.

This is a free, self-timed, unsupported adventure.

We provide the route, a suggested start time, and a finish line in Birdeye.

You provide the legs, the logistics, the navigation, the snacks, and whatever it takes to get yourself home.

Your bike. Your pace. Your adventure.

THE REWARD

There is no giant trophy.

No cash prize.

No podium.

The reward is finishing something that looked a little ridiculous when you signed up.

It's the satisfaction of covering the miles, solving the problems, pushing through the hard parts, and rolling back into Birdeye under your own power.  

And, of course, making it back in time for dinner.

Finish the route and add your name to the short list of Birdeye Ultra finishers.

FIND OUT WHAT YOU'RE MADE OF.

Ride with friends.
Push the pace.
Race somebody who wants to race.
Or disappear down the road and make it a solo mission.

Use it as training for your next big one, a bikepacking adventure with your buds, or simply as an excuse to do something completely unreasonable.

However you choose to ride it, we're here to stoke the fire.

THE ROUTES

BIRDEYE 500 Route

NIGHT OWL 200 Route

Looking for beta?
Explore the Crowley’s Ridge Gravel Trail route collection.

Important: These are unofficial routes. Route conditions can change. You are responsible for your own navigation, safety, equipment, food, water, and logistics. Trackleaders registration is required: https://form.jotform.com/trackleaders/birdeye26

There is NO rolling SAG.

If you need a bailout, call your bestie.

THE CLOCK IS YOURS.

Start whenever you want.

Leave Birdeye on any date and at any time that works for your adventure.

The only requirement:

Be back in Birdeye by dinner on Saturday, November 7.

That's your finish line.

THE SELFIE BONUS

Hit the Arkansas State Parks along the route?

Prove it.

Post your State Park selfies, tag Studio Drift, and you'll be entered to win prizes.

Ride the miles. Collect the parks. Tell the story.

MORE THAN A RIDE

Birdeye Ultra is part of studioDRIFT's mission to build a stronger Arkansas Delta through outdoor recreation and community.

Your participation helps studioDRIFT continue investing in trails, outdoor recreation, cultural programming, and the rural communities that make the Delta special.

Welcome to the Third NYC Velo Fire Tower Brevet (FT3)!  A special thanks to the folks that helped us put this together:

The Team at NYC Velo

Search and State All Road Apparel

Chris McNally Drawing Studio

We're following up the success of the first 2 editions of the Fire Tower Brevet (thanks to all of you who took part!) with a new route & 5 new towers!  The new route spends little time in our beloved Hudson Valley, opting for adventures westward.  This new uncharted terrain (by Fire Tower Brevet standards) includes immersion in the New Jersey Highlands, the Delaware Valley, and the Pocono Mountains of Pennsylvania.  The new route for FT3 explores notable areas of Northern NJ & Eastern PA: Hackensack & Patterson NJ, High Mountain Park, Jungle Habitat, High Point State Park, Stairway Wild Area, Hickory Run Forest, Hell Mountain, and, notably, Staten Island.  While there are some lengthy sections of flat terrain, the 5 Fire Tower ascents include gradients, often unpaved, that can exceed 20% (all 5 tower ascents this year are rideable, apologies again for the gut punch that was Mt Beacon).  Though it may be argued that this ride isn't for everyone we've made accommodations so that those of you uninterested in a death march in the mountains can still enjoy a great adventure:

  • The goal of the Fire Tower Brevet is to push the limits a bit of Brevet-style riding and to explore parts of the Mid-Atlantic & Hudson Valley regions that may be off the radar of NYC cyclists.  Scroll down for details of the ride & prizes, and links to the route. The ride is Brevet-style, starting and ending at NYC Velo - East Village (66 2nd Avenue)
  • The 5 Controles (checkpoints) on the route are 5 historical Fire Towers throughout Northern NJ & the Pocono Mountains of Pennsylvania, chosen for their location and bike accessibility, these include:
    • Ramapo Station Fire Tower (Heart hole punch)
    • Buckhorn Ridge Fire Tower (Rectangle hole punch)
    • High Knob Fire Tower (Star hole punch)
    • Pohopoco Fire Tower (Diamond hole punch)
    • Mauch Chunk (Bear Mountain) Fire Tower (Circle hole punch)
  • The "Suggested Route" is approximately 330 miles. Riders are not required to follow the route, only to visit the 5 Controles
  • Riders who plan to participate are required to register here on BikeReg and will be issued a Brevet card (designed by the artist Chris McNally)
  • At each Controle there will be a uniquely-shaped hole punch used to punch the corresponding Fire Tower on the Brevet card
  • Riders will also produce digital proof of successful Controle check-in/route completion (via a GPS/Strava file and/or Instagram/social media photos of themselves at the Controle) to qualify for the tiered Rewards
  • The official ride start is 5:00am Saturday July 11 2026 at NYC Velo East Village though riders may complete their own adventure at anytime between July 11 and 11:59pm October 31 2026
  • This is an unsupported ride – riders are responsible for their own navigation, hydration, nutrition, equipment, and safety - the use of e-bikes, cars, trains, etc are prohibited for Tier 1 & Tier 2 consideration
  • Riders should take appropriate caution riding on open roads, use appropriate lighting for low light or night time riding conditions, and use appropriate safety gear at all times (including helmets, reflective apparel, etc)

 

The Suggested Route:

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/55755950
 


The Tiers of Participation:

  1. Tier 1 Participation: Riders must start and end at NYC Velo East Village and complete all 5 Controles within 48 hours.  Riders may follow any route but may use only 1 human-powered bicycle (i.e. no e-bikes, trains, or Ubers).  Riders who complete the course (starting & ending at NYC Velo East Village) and collect punches at the 5 Controles in any 48-hour period from opening day (July 11) through October 31 2026 will present documentation to Andrew at NYC Velo East Village or by emailing info@nycvelo.com.
  2. Tier 2 Participation: riders complete the course in 1 continuous ride but take longer than 48 hours but less than 120 hours -- for example if they want to expand the route to take 4 or 5 days and visit other locations in the Catskills, or they simply want to stretch the ride across more days (starting & ending at NYC Velo East Village).  Tier 2 Participation will be open through October 31 2026.
  3. Tier 3 Participation: riders complete all 5 Controles on separate visits over any length of time (weeks or months), but always by bike.  Controles may be completed over separate outings and in any order.  Tier 3 Participation will be open through October 31 2026.  

Rewards:

  1. For successful Tier 1 completion: Coleman Camp of Type 3 in Brooklyn has come on board to make custom Musette Bags, available for the first 20 riders to successfully complete the Tier 1 challenge.  Tier 1 winners will also receive a custom Fire Tower Brevet enamel pin and sticker pack.
  2. For successful Tier 2 completion: NYC Velo will send out a custom Fire Tower Brevet enamel pin, sticker pack, & Search and State cycling cap (limited to the first 50 riders)
  3. For successful Tier 3 completion: NYC Velo will send out a Fire Tower Brevet sticker pack (Tier 3 is unlimited)

Additional Ride Notes:

 
Though it's assumed that all who have signed up for this adventure are seasoned and thoughtful riders, riders are implored to make safely their highest consideration when attempting the Third Fire Tower Brevet:
  • Always have appropriate lighting on you and your bike during low or no-light situations
  • Pay close attention to your hydration and nutrition plan & stay hydrated
  • Please be aware of the dangers of over heating/heat exhaustion -- trust that this ride isn't worth it

NOTE that as of Thursday 7/9 all hole punches were attached to their respective towers.  It is possible that this may change as time goes on and other punches disappear - if that happens just document your visit to the tower (i.e. Ramapo Station, etc) with a selfie - there is a backup set of punches in the shop and you can get your card punched after the fact, just record the time with a photo (and send it to info@nycvelo.com) for credit of the Controle.
  • Be sure to tag @nycvelo and #firetowerbrevet & #FT3 on your social media posts -- thanks!
  • Be prepared with insect repellent during the ride -- you'll be swarmed by biting insects (flies, mosquitos, etc) on some sections of the route, especially on the climbs where you can't outrun them
  • I again implore people attempting this course to keep the temperature conditions, hydration and nutrition front of mind as there are food (& hydration) deserts outside of the city and major highways and many things close early in the mountains
Extra Credit:
 
Maybe it's because we've been working on this ride for so long, but we have a list of some additional can't miss things close to the "suggested" Fire Tower Brevet route.  Any registered rider who accomplishes any of the items below during their attempt at the Brevet and posts a photo of it on social media (be sure to tag @nycvelo so that I see it) will get a separate Brevet patch:
  • The first “Extra Credit” is so important that it should just be considered “Credit” – visit the High Point of NJ – it's on the route!
  • Grab a coffee or bite to eat at Abraço (81 East 7th STreet in the East Village, @abraco_espresso)
  • Make a rubbing of a Geological Survey Marker at any point on or near the course
  • Add some additional climbing on the ride (but you can deviate from the route if you like) to reach a total elevation gain of 29,032 feet (a form of "Everesting" without the 24-hour time limit)
  • Spend the night camping at a lean-to along the route.
Enjoy the ride!

For the eleventh year, Yellow Chip Road is going SPOOKY! Formerly know as Ill Kanza, this is a long running grassroots gravel grinder starting and ending in Kansas, Illinois. In contrast to the recent trend of making gravel events smoother and easier, our routes remain as gnarly as ever! Expect varied surfaces including some very rough gravel and stream crossings, rolling terrain, and remote scenery. The 104 mile route in particular has some especially rough and rocky sections, though none of the routes are easy. All routes will be timed, with prizes for the top three in each category of the 3 longest routes. All entries get raffle tickets! This event will be mostly self supported. Make sure to bring spare tubes, a pump or CO2, tools, and ideally chain quick links. We will have a number you can call if you really cannot continue but for the most part riders are expected to fix problems on their own.
 
There will be two supply tables with drop bag service, supply table A and supply table B. Most courses will only visit one of them. We will collect drop bags before the event that we will run out to each table. There will be one additional supply table on the 104 mile course. We will also have some additional food and water available to all at the tables. Here is the mile marker that each table is at on each course:

We will put a sign at every turn that is on a gravel road and not at a T-intersection. The course will also be marked with pavement markings (on paved roads) and flags (everywhere). Rapture in Misery: From 24 Hours of Madness to a Mountain Biking Legend

Celebrating the legacy of a race that became a rite of passage

It Started with a Wild Idea

In 2001, a loose-knit group of mountain bikers rolled into Snow Creek chasing something few could understand — and even fewer could finish. A 24-hour mountain bike race. No glory, no fame — just headlights, hills, and a lot of pain. The idea was simple: ride until you can't, then ride a little more.

That first Rapture in Misery lit a fire. And soon, it became more than just a race. It became a legend.

The First Ride – Snow Creek, 2001

There was something gritty and pure about that first year. Snow Creek, typically known for its winter ski runs, played host to a summer sufferfest. Riders took turns circling a course that felt more like an endurance gauntlet than a bike race. People rode through the night, relying on duct tape, drive, and caffeine to hold themselves together.

There were no luxuries — just tents, cold sandwiches, and the sound of freehubs clicking through the darkness. If you were there, you still tell stories about it. If you weren’t, you’ve heard them.

Landahl Park – Technical, Raw, and Wild

After two years at Snow Creek, Rapture in Misery moved to Landahl Park, one of Missouri’s most revered singletrack trail systems. And with that shift, the race found a new kind of identity: raw, technical, and beautifully brutal.

Landahl’s terrain was a whole different animal. Tight turns, sharp climbs, off-camber descents — it wasn’t just about endurance anymore. It was about skill, timing, and knowing exactly how hard you could push without breaking... your bike or yourself.

Some came because they loved Landahl’s unforgiving charm. Others came because they’d heard about this crazy race where legends were made — and sometimes broken. Either way, it was a proving ground, and it helped cement Rapture as a must-do for Midwest endurance junkies.

Crowder State Park – Community Roots Deepen

Eventually, Rapture moved again in 2009 — this time to Crowder State Park, and with that move came a new phase. If Snow Creek was the spark and Landahl the fire, Crowder was where the fire turned into a tradition.

At Crowder, the vibe shifted from wild experiment to beloved annual gathering. The course was tough — don’t let anyone tell you otherwise — but there was something about it that brought people together. The campground felt like a mini-village each year, full of familiar faces, shared meals, and the occasional beer hand-up.

It was here that Rapture’s community really bloomed. Solo riders, team riders, rookies, and veterans all came together with a shared understanding: this race was something special.

More Than a Race – What Made RIM Special

What set Rapture in Misery apart wasn’t just the course, the miles, or the midnight hallucinations — it was the people.

There was something magnetic about the event that brought out the best (and sometimes the weirdest) in everyone. You’d see solo riders grinding out lap after lap with thousand-yard stares, and then laugh at a guy in a tutu sprinting for a handoff. You’d share tools, tubes, and war stories with people you’d just met.

It was more than a race. It was a reunion for the unreasonably driven — the community of “why-not?” people. Everyone suffered, and everyone smiled through it.

The Newest Chapter

Well HEY!  Another of year of the greatest race in the Land o' MABRA (yes, we own our bias).  

Welcome to Baltimore Youth Cycling's Frosty Cross!  We are proud to once again be hosting the MABRA Age Graded Championships!

We’re glad you'll be joining us.  This year we are back at the Agricultural Center: the same great venue and awesome course (can’t wait to see what our course designer comes up with this year).   

This year we are introducing wave starts!

All riders in a wave will start on a single whistle and results that are sent to USA Cycling will be based on the wave, not on the individual categories. Podiums and prizes at the event WILL BE broken out by category. We repeat, All riders in a wave will start on a single whistle and results that are sent to USA Cycling will be based on the wave, not on the individual categories. Podiums and prizes at the event WILL BE broken out by category.

Why are we doing this? For a few reasons – first and foremost, we believe it provides a better race experience for everyone. Riders in races with multiple classes will start based on Cross Results point meaning a rider starting on a second whistle won’t have to work through the slower riders from the first whistle right after their start. For categories with fewer riders, it means a more competitive race and a chance to work on your race-craft instead of riding around the course with only a few riders. Secondly, it provides a better opportunity for riders to earn points and better their USAC ranking. USAC points will be scored based on the wave rather than the individual field. For riders in smaller fields, this means a chance to earn points where no points would have been awarded for the smaller field. For all riders, you have the chance to earn points based on a larger pool of riders (and thus USAC points).

Location:

The Center for Maryland Agriculture is located at 1114 Shawan Rd Cockeysville, MD 21030 about one mile west of I-83. It's conveniently located a few minutes away from Hunt Valley, where you will find hotels, restaurants, coffee shops, and any other services you might need.  We have ample on-site parking.

Looking forward to a great day!!!  We've put an order in for great weather (definition of this may vary by racer).

NOTES: 

This event is held under USA Cycling permit.  All USA Cycling Cyclocross rules apply.

    •    A USAC racing license is required for all races except the kids' race (racers 8 and under).  If you do not supply a valid license # at registration you will be charged an extra $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This type of license is valid for entry only in races that are open to Novice (Cat. 5) riders.

    •    Mountain bikes are allowed; however, bar ends are NOT allowed and must be removed.
    •    MABRA Cyclocross Series rules available at http://www.mabra.org/
    •    There will be a $10 day-of surcharge added to the entry fees shown above.
    •    Junior riders ONLY may enter any non-age-graded adult race they qualify for by category at the Junior price by entering coupon code FRX_2025_JRS at checkout.
    •    Payout Parity: Top five finishers in the Men’s 1/2/3 race receive the same amount in payout as the Women’s 1/2/3. 

    •    Event will be held rain or shine.
Thanks to Gross Mendelsohn for sponsoring our elite podiums!

Warmups: The course will be open for inspection and warm-up approximately 15 minutes prior to each event. Warming up on the course during an event is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated. DQ & forfeiture of entry fee will result.

Call-Ups: Staging will be based on the most recent Cross-Results score

    1.    All pre-registered riders will be staged on the grid, by bib number.  Bib numbers will be assigned as follows, according to ranking on CrossResults.com as of the close of registration.
    2.    Remaining riders will be staged by bib number, in the order of registration.

Those classes consisting of only cat 5 men or cat 4 women are staged by order of registration. All day-of registrants will be staged behind pre-registered riders.

Transgender policy: 

Baltimore Youth Cycling welcomes everyone to participate in the gender category they feel is most appropriate to them, as described in USA Cycling policies: https://usacycling.org/about-us/governance/transgender-athletes-policy

Women may enter any men’s race for which they are eligible by age, category, and any performance requirements. They may also enter categorized races for men that are up to one category lower than their women’s category. Category 1 women may enter men’s races up to two categories lower.

Master women may compete in men’s master's races as follows:

Category 1 and 2 master women may enter men’s events for riders up to 10 years above their racing ages;
Category 3 and 4 master women may enter men’s events for riders up to 20 years above their racing ages.

Results:  Baltimore Youth Cycling’s Frosty Cross is electronically timed. The protest period is a firm 15 minutes from the announcement that results have been posted. Racers are also reminded to make sure their team name is correct in USA Cycling, BikeReg, and on the waiver at the race.

EventNotes:
Element Adventures is proud to present Gritventure! 2, an adventure ride based out of our Element Adventures West Camp in Augusta, WV.  Featuring quiet gravel roads, stiff climbs, beautiful vistas, and backcountry riding, this ride will bring out the little kid in you!  This route will provide you with a tough challenge, but it will be well worth it!   Route details are below.

This will be a true gravel adventure: minimal SAG support, no route markings.  Download the GPX files so you can navigate the route (Cue sheets will also be provided).  There will be no aid stations set up, though there will be bars and gels available at the ride start to throw in your jersey pockets to take with you.  You'll need to carry enough water with you to last the ride or refill at stores or spigots found along the way.  You can refill bottles on the route at the Grassy Lick Kirby Community Center at a spigot.  Be prepared with flat changing tools and spare tubes, as gravel can be rough on tires (Some of the "roads" are now two grooves of singletrack!).  Take a cell phone, but be aware that service can be spotty.  This ride will go rain or shine, and being fall, there is always chance that it will be chilly and rainy.  Be prepared!

Suggested Equipment: A cyclocross or gravel / adventure bike with at least 32-40 mm tires would be your best choice.  A mountain bike would not even be out of place, especially on Short Mountain and Nathaniel Mountain for the Long and Medium routes.  You'll want a wide range of gearing, too, as some of the hills can be steep.  Helmets are required for all participants.

Cost: $25 through Oct 24, then $35 through Oct 30.  Day of registration will be $45.

Time: Check-in will be at 8:00 am through 10:00 am.  We will have a group start time of 8:30am if you would like to ride with the group.  You do not need to stay with the group. 

Food! Be sure to stay for the food and beer after the ride!

Directions to Element Adventures West Camp: From NoVA, take I-66 West to I-81 North to exit 310 (Route 37).  Take 37 North to Route 50 West.  Take Route 50 West through Augusta, WV.  Make a left onto McKee Hollow Road.  Take an almost immediate right onto South Fork of Little Cacapon Road.  In about 1.2 miles you will see a large mailbox with the address 1332.  Turn right up the driveway, and follow all the way up past the house and the barn to the parking area.  (Google Maps of South Fork of Little Cacapon road brings you just short of the address - you'll go a bit further to reach the driveway).  There will be an Element Adventures sign at the driveway.

 

Jerseys: Pre-order a jersey to commemorate this great ride!  These jerseys are full-zip and made of advanced moisture-wicking fabric to keep you cool and dry.  Rear pockets. Comfortable club fit available in mens and womens. You can order your jersey during registration.  $75. Size Charts below.

About the Regional Food Bank:

The Regional Food Bank has been helping to feed the poor and hungry in our communities since 1982. It is the only organization of its kind in northeastern New York. The Food Bank collects large donations of food from the food industry and distributes it to charitable agencies serving hungry and disadvantaged people in 23 counties. From Plattsburgh to Newburgh, in urban, rural, and suburban communities, the Food Bank provides over 55 million pounds of food a year to 1,000 agencies. The Food Bank is a member of Feeding America, the national network of food banks. The Regional Food Bank is a non-profit organization, and all donations are tax-deductible to the fullest extent of the law.

Sunday November 1st 2026 is going to be a day to remember. We’re proud to bring you Cyclocross at Grand Island's premier Beaver Island State Park for yet another year. This place has all the goods including WNY’s best cyclocross sand pit, mixed riding surfaces, rolling terrain and beautiful waterfront views. Can you ride the beach? There’s only one way to find out! The history of Cyclocross at Beaver Island goes all the way back to Brenden Conway's Beaver Island Black Out! in 2012, No one who was there that day will ever forget that experience... 

Join us for a great day on the bike or spectating with friends and family. Beaver CX is not USAC Sanctioned so you do not need a race license to participate. Why would we do that? We wanted to reduce the barriers to entry. No race license means no extra fees for new racers. Less confusion and complications for our Canadian friends willing to cross the border. No reason not to come out of retirement if you happen to be an “experienced” racer that hasn't renewed their license for a couple years. All in all, a lot of reasons to race, very few reasons not to!

Racing will start at 10:30am with a course designed specifically for our Junior racers and continue through our final race of the day ending at or around 2pm. 

We will allow day of registration but ask you to please pre-register if possible. These events take many volunteers to run successfully and any and all preparation that can be done ahead of time makes these days run much smoother. Double up and race a second race for only $15! 

Back for 2026: The Buffalo cyclocross promotors have teamed up with The Campus Cycling Collective (the organizer of this race) to bring you The Rust Belt Ruckus! : A Buffalo Cyclocross Series This will be race 3 of 5 in the series. The Stump Farm Mountain Bike Races are back for 2026 on November 1.   The 20 mile, three lap comp event starts at 10:00 and the one lap race starts at 10:10 for the FAT BIKE Category and 10:15 for the one lap 7 mile..  We have a mix of two track trail for passing and leaf blown single track on a full 7 mile plus loop. The Race direction in 2026 generally follows for the Normal trail flow; Counter Clockwise on the map with some added 2 track for passing early in the loop.

This is a small race with field limits so register early. Accordingly, there are no refunds for any reason.  Your registration is final. There are overall and age group awards.

Number plate pickup and concessions are inside the lodge.  We need the number plates back for the 2027 race.  Please help us with that!   

We ask you to self-seed in your start and be aware that the first transition to single track comes after a 0.8 mile roll out just like our August race, Refo Ramble.

We will leaf blow the course on Saturday, a bonus for all our area riders!  There are no aid stations.  We will have mobile course marshals and a medical cart.  

So, bring your own feeds for the race.  We will have Ahnapee Beer free if you show us a trail pass.  Garbage is carry in, carry out. 

Brown County is great at maintaining our trails with the help of the Friends of the Reforestation Camp Trails, one of your hosts!. To ride the trails, the County requires a daily or annual pass. For your convenience, if you don't have an annual pass already, you can pay us $5 below and show the ranger your receipt if you are asked. Otherwise you can buy a pass online or on site on race day or at the sign board just outside the lodge with a card or exact change. Trail fees support the trails.  We like that!  We will give you a beer/coffee ticket if you show us a trail pass as a thank you.  

Course marking will occur Friday to reinforce normal flow. There is no foot race this year.

The event host is the Green Bay Trailblazers, with Friends of the Reforestation Camp Trails,  and Ashwaubenon Nordic Ski Team partnering again.  Your race volunteers are the from FoRCT, Trailblazers and ANST.

Course Description:

WE'RE BACK FOR OUR 14TH YEAR! and excited to announce that the Fourteethn edition of WCCX will be held on Sunday November 1st at famous Ludwig’s Corner Horse Show and Fairgrounds.  This location has special history...utilized by Wissahickon Cross (including UCI races) for several years last held in 2009, and more recently the home of WCCX since 2018.  For 2026, WCCX is celebrating it's 14th anniversary!

As you may remember this site is very spectator friendly, with the entire course being visible from the promanade hill.  It also has easy to access of the PA Turnpike and will exceed the high level of racer expectations that come with a WCCX event.  Don't miss the 14th year for WCCX cyclocross.  Classic cyclocross course with two sets of barriers and variable terrain mostly grass, with some gravel. EventNotes:
The Dirty Pilgrim

A Gravel Ride for the People!

Although over shadowed by less significant events at the time, upon their arrival in Plymouth the Pilgrims found more than a mere "rock" upon which they hoped to land all their dreams. Rather, they found a rich & diverse countryside laced with miles of idyllic gravel roads, accented by scenic vistas, and punctuated with an abundance of fine craft brews & richly roasted coffee. Building upon that spirit of adventure & excitement that they felt that day, we now present for your entertainment and pedaling enjoyment, The Dirty Pilgrim. 

Ladies & gentlemen, early-risers & thrill seekers, snack enthusiasts & coffee fiends... Let us all now go in peace and Pedal in Dirt.  May the Grit Be With You.  

-Amen

About:
The Dirty Pilgrim is the brainchild of longtime South Shore gravel aficionados Steve Cobble, Brian Carlson, & Dave Farrell. They're constantly looking to explore old trails, find new routes to ride, and always doing so with with less pavement involved.  Now although some group led rides will be available, in general you should be comfortable with self-navigating via GPS or plan on riding with someone who is.  To that end, be sure to bring ample food & water, spare tubes & inflators, a fully charged cell phone, and a healthy “can do” attitude.  We'll see you out there!

**Navigation:
There will be NO course markings. Riders are required to download the supplied routes below and load on your GPS OR ride on event day with one of our group led rides.   There will be bailouts for the Advanced and Epic routes - take note the mile marker if you want to follow different route back.

A checkpoint-style ride to the hidden gems of Chittenden County

Here’s the situation, it’s November 1st, the leaves have fallen, the days are getting shorter, but you’re looking for one last adventure ride. Well, your friends at Jericho Dirt have a new type of adventure ride for you, inspired by the LA Tourist events in Southern California. 
 

Here’s the deal, there will be a start and finish location, but no set route. A few days before the event all participants will be sent GPS coordinates and clues for checkpoints at some of our favorite places, where books are hidden. At each checkpoint you will need to find the book, rip out the page corresponding to your number plate. Once you have collected all of the pages, you return to the finish destination and turn them in for a finish time. You’re free to take any route you like and connect the checkpoints in any order. Want to add in a scenic detour or favorite shortcut, go for it. The only rules are: you must complete the course under your own power on one bike (no uber, no bus rides, no bike swaps), follow all laws, and respect private property, trail, or road closures. 


Bike choice and route choice are half the challenge. While most races will tell you exactly where to go and what bike you must ride, this format leaves the choice up to you. There will checkpoints that favor a road bike, while others may favor a gravel bike, and maybe one or two where you want a MTB. The route you choose can make one type of bike preferable over another. Some might choose to ride a road bike and hike any single track they encounter, others might choose the comfort and capability of a mountain bike. Generally a gravel bike is likely the most efficient, but that may differ based on your individual route and skills. 

There will be a long option, expect 55-75 miles, and a short option with fewer checkpoints, 25-40 miles. You can ride with as many friends as you like or roll solo. 

Once you make it to the finish, with or without all your pages, you will be greeted by a local hotdog and beer from Lucy and Howe brewery, included in your entry. Feel free to hangout and share adventure stories with your fellow riders.

  • 9:00 - Rider Roll - Out

  • 12:00 - 5:00 - Hot Dogs and Beer as you arrive back from your ride 
     

Special note: Please do not park at the Jericho Ale and Bean/Lucy and Howe as they have limited parking. You can park at the Jericho Elementary School which is a short (0.4 mi) walk/ride from the brewery.

It's Heidi Rentz & Zander Ault here...

We are co-creators of The Spirit World 100 & The Cyclist's Menu, gravel cyclists, chefs & party animals. We're so freaking excited to see you in Patagonia, Arizona for a gravel road race that has inspired every aspect of our lives.

The Arizona Borderlands are known for it's rugged, stunning landscapes & views that you'd never guess existed. You have to see it with your own eyes! Throughout the Spirit World 30, 50, 80, & 100 mile courses - you'll climb up + down & around elevations that range between 4,000 - 6,000 feet above sea level. The San Rafael Valleys demanding terrain asks that you keep your head up at all times. EventNotes:
Welcome to BikeReg Online Registration

Registration is OPEN !!!   

(Registration Closes Thursday 11/06/26 12Noon)

for

11th Anniversary of Nevada County Women's MTB Skills Clinic and Camp  

This is a 2 day MTB skills clinic, 

or 

a 1 day MTB skills clinic with an add-on option Sunday for advanced skills

Spread the word!   

Before starting on-line BikeReg registration, determine your rider level from the program.pdf and read our refund policy.

 

With miles cross country and enduro trails, and home of TDS Enduro, TDS Ranch is our venue choice for learning mountain bike skill clinics designed to inspire, strengthen, build confidence and show that mountain biking is a sport for everyone!  Mountain biking enriches your mind, body, soul and opens the door to meeting more women in the biking community.  Learn bike handling skills, increase your confidence, enjoyment learning with others, and trail love when riding your bike.  We raised the bar with Specialized Bike demo bikes available at our clinic!

Proceeds support Nevada County youth bike clubs (~400 youth) and Gateway Bike Park Phase 2 Build in Penn Valley, California.

Our amazing 2026 coaching cadre:

  1. Pro Racer Amy Morrison, National and World Titles, NICA Nevada League Head Coach, Carson City, Nevada
  2. Pro Racer Tasha Thomas, California Enduro Series OA Titles, USA Cycling Coach, S.Lake Tahoe, California
  3. Kristen Del Campo, BICP Certified Instructor, Kings Beach, California,
  4. Jessica Tseng, Meet Jessica Tseng, Epiphany Trails, San Jose, California,

We have a robust program for women to improve their learning experience at various skill stations, each with various background to teach beginners the basics, and fine tune those missing tiny improvements for advanced riders.  You'll feel more confident off or on your bike, you’ll fine tune bike handling techniques, body positions for various riding conditions/features, and more.  Enjoy our healthy snacks, gourmet meals, and our Nevada County hospitality.  Plus our raffle drawing!  See clinic & meal photos at our FB album:

https://www.facebook.com/NevadaCountyWomenMTBCC/photos

Our instructors are from northern California and Nevada who instruct and coach, race downhill, enduro, cross-country, cyclo-cross, and part of the movement connecting school bike club youth to learn that mountain biking as an awesome sport.  So ..... plan ahead to enjoy a weekend to build your mountain bike skills and network with more shredders who have the dirt passion !!!   Start your list of questions like you hit a wall and can't get to the next level for rides, racing,  nutrition, etc. for our cadre.   We understand this is an expensive cost and we need to pay our instructors and event costs.  Please review the below 2026 MTB Skills Clinic Fee Schedule:

  • $275 Saturday MTB Skills Clinic and Meals
  • $250 Saturday MTB Skills Clinic and No Meals
  • $175 Add-On Sunday MTB Skills Clinic and No Meals (Saturday MTB Skills Clinic Required)
  • $30/night Optional dry camping at venue for RV's, vans, trailers, tents (bring your own water, potty rentals at venue)
  • MTB skills clinic includes, instructors, fees, t-shirt, permits, insurance, rentals, supplies, venue, meals (or no meals).
    • Note:  If you change your mind about meals or add-on Sunday MTB skills clinic sign-ups, please bring cash.

 

Complete custom questions for meal prep!….This helps have an organized weekend from event pint glass order, meal planning, and those dry camping Friday and/or Saturday nights (3pm Check-in).   PLEASE answer ALL questions so we meet your special dietary needs.   Meal plan is weather dependent.  Saturday and Sunday MTB clinics start at 9am.  This allows participants to eat a hearty breakfast at home or on the road.  

 

Click event webpage link for tentative weekend schedule and meal details in the weekend program.pdf. at: https://ybonc.org/events/mountain-bike-clinic/

 

Last but not least, there is poison oak along sections of TDS trails even in the fall and winter (branches with no leaves).  Bring extra shoes/clothes to change out of in case you rubbed against any vines or branches, and plastic bags for post ride clothes for wet clothes.  We will have TechNu packets at registration table.  We have outdoor heaters to keep you warm on breaks too!

 

Swag Stuff!  Oh yeah, our swag bag is loaded.  2 raffle tickets (drawing on Sunday) with bike industry products from our sponsors.  Raffle is U-Pick!

 

This weekend is all about you … Rain or Shine … So Let’s Roll Ladies on 2026 Nov. 7-8 !!!

Requirement:  Complete registration, event waiver, bring bike, helmet, gloves, water bottle/hydration system, water proof or poncho to stay dry for wet weather trail conditions, camping chair, layers of clothing to stay warm (jacket/gloves/hat/neck gaiter) around campfire.   We have propane heaters and canopies to keep us warm and dry when not riding.  When was the last time your bike was serviced?  If your bike has not been serviced recently, please have your bike inspected at your local bike shop to prevent mechanical issues during the event weekend...brakes, chain, tires, etc.  

 

Volunteering?  

Unfortunately registered participants cannot sign-up to volunteer.  From past clinics, participants forget or arrive late for volunteer tasks.  We want you to learn as much as possible from our MTB instructors.  Volunteering does not waive or reduce registration event fee.  Volunteers for clinic groups required to be a intermediate rider and know TDS trails.

 

Note: 

  • We recommend Best Western Gold Country Inn (or a new Holiday Express if open),, Grass Valley
    • More lodging options:
      • https://www.nevadacitychamber.com/nevada-city-hotels-and-lodging/
  • Full RV/Camper Hook-ups at:
    • https://nevadacountyfair.com/rv-park/
    • https://inntowncampground.com/
  • This is a USAC sanction event as a training clinic

 

Participant Waitlist:

Yes, we have a waitlist option at BikeReg registration.  Only add your name to with waitlist if you are sure you can attend.  Because on-line BikeReg registration closes on 11/05/26 Sunday, call (530) 513-7852 so we can confirm you will be attending if a spot opens up.  Please bring cash when you check-in Saturday morning and complete participant event waiver.   

 

Refund Policy:

Why do we have a cancellation policy?
This event is a fundraiser for YBONC Foundation Programs supporting rural Nevada County youth.  We do not issue refunds or transfer registrations for our fundraiser events.  An event participant's registration can be reimbursed as a comp code toward the following year skills clinic, or as a donation to our foundation.  Our cancellation policy reflects the fact that the closer it is to the event dates, the more challenging it is to adjust plans, and the less likely to find someone to take an open spot.  

For any registered participant unable to attend due to injury, illness, or personal reason, please forward your event registration confirmation email to us AND request for the following year event's comp code or state you would like to donate your event registration to our foundation.  Please send individual email per participant, not combined participant emails, to:
Send email to:     yboncfdn@gmail.com
Subject Line:  
Cancellation Notice for MM/DD/YY of First & Last Name of Participant - Request Comp 
Code or Making a Donation


We set event dates a year in advance with clinic instructors, land owner, and plan locations dependent on trails, weather, fire, etc. to create an exceptional experience for every participant, and set things up with the 
expectation that each day will be fun with MTB skills and networking.  We are focused to host a great 
mountain bike skills clinic for women.

•    If severe weather or fires cancels event, participants will receive a BikeReg event cancellation email.  Event cancellation are posted on event FB/IG feeds too.  If forecast is light rain, we will still host event as we have canopies and propane heaters to keep participants warm and dry during breaks and meals.  This is the only case we issue event registrations to participants. 
•    No refunds as event payments are made in advance for costs such as insurance, permits, instructors, product orders, swags/bling, food, instructors, etc.  A registered participant may outreach to someone to fill their spot and arrange payment method themselves, or gift their entry.  Please FORWARD your confirmation BikeReg email with the person's info who is replacing your spot (First & Last Name, cell no. and mailing address.)   

Disclaimer:

As event planning occurs a year in advance, the event organizer is authorized to change event details.  It is the participant's responsibility to revisit the event webpage for latest details 1 week prior to the event weekend.

 

Thank you! 

Jet Lowe,

Event Organizer

Birdeye ’26 is fun-filled weekend in the heart of the Arkansas Delta—where remote gravel roads, big skies, live music, and good food come together for one unforgettable experience. 

Whether you're looking for a challenging ride or just a reason to casually explore somewhere new, Birdeye is your invitation to come see the Delta differently. Check out this slideshow. 

COME FOR THE ADVENTURE

Choose from multiple gravel routes designed to showcase the unique terrain, quiet roads, small communities, and beautiful landscapes of Crowley’s Ridge. From first-timers to experienced gravel riders, there's a route for you. Ride hard. Ride curious. Ride somewhere unexpected. Check out this route collection.

STAY FOR THE PARTY

Come back to the farm for food, drinks, music, and a proper Delta weekend.  Two nights. Two artists. One unforgettable setting. 

FRIDAY · WILL COPPAGE 

Americana, Delta storytelling, and soulful songwriting. 

SATURDAY · BEAR RYAN 

Texas country, Delta blues, and Southern rock ’n’ roll. Small crowd. Big music. Under the Delta sky. 

WHY BIRDEYE? 

Because some of the best adventures in Arkansas happen over here. Birdeye is hosted by studioDRIFT, a nonprofit working to  expand access to outdoor recreation throughout the Arkansas Delta. Your participation helps support the Crowley’s Ridge Gravel Trail and the people and places that make the Delta magical. 

Come for the fun. Stay for the weekend. Leave changed.

The Event

Address - 2813 Jerusalem Mill Road, Kingsville MD 21087

6 Hours at the Mill is a 6 hour individual, duo or team relay race. If you are looking for a fun, laid-back, low-cost, competitive experience where the proceeds go to a few awesome non-profit organizations, then sign up before we reach the 150 racer cap. The approximately five mile long course is challenging but approachable for all ages and skill levels.

October Quiz and Lottery to Win 50% Off Registration

The October quiz question can be found at https://forms.gle/gLCH3htLUSacNMX16 . Each person who answers the question correctly will be place into a lottery. The person selected from the lottery will win 50% off registration or be refunded 50% of the registration cost. This final quiz also contains a bonus question for a second entrance into the lottery. Good luck!

Social Media Updates

For updates please see our Facebook page at https://www.facebook.com/6-Hours-at-the-Mill-100083232973843/ 

Volunteer

Not racing, but want to volunteer. Sign up at https://volunteersignup.org/HBEH7 

It takes a lot of volunteers to make this event happen and we can really use your help with parking, registration, and course marshalling.

Food Truck

Kooper's Chowhound Burger Wagon will be on hand to serve up an assortment of hand held burgers including vegetarian options. You can find them at http://www.brgrwagon.com/ 

The Course

The course is a roughly 5 mile loop with 588 feet of climbing per lap. The course starts relatively flat in the rolling fields of Jerusalem Mill and then narrows a bit as the course gains elevation as it enters into the wooded mixture of singletrack and doubletrack. The course consists of rugged classic East Coast single track. Roots, rocks, significant elevation gains, stream crossings, etc. make for a technical challenge on the first leg of the course. Second half of the course is mostly downhill and / or flat giving a reprieve before returning to the pits and starting the roughly 5 mile loop over. Pits and start / finish area will be in grassy open fields. 

Preliminary race lap information can be found at https://www.trailforks.com/routepopular/81337289/ This is close to the final course, but there will be a few slight changes. The file will be updated to reflect any changes to the course.

Race Duration

The race begins at 9:00am EST with a mass wave start. All solo, duo, and team races are the same duration. Racers, or teams of racers, will complete as many laps as possible by the end time, 3:00pm EST. Racers in the same field with the same number of laps will be scored based on lowest total elapsed race time.

Team Pits

Solo, Duo, and Teams may set up a pit along the course in the field. Team tents (EZ-Up style canopy tents) are permitted, but please take care to anchor tents sufficiently if there are strong winds forecast on race day. Pit selection will occur on a first come, first served basis. While a food truck will be on hand, please be sure to bring enough water and food for the duration of the event.

Relay Transitions

Duo and Team categories are relay races. Scoring and timing will not identify individual racer by name so if you want to know your individual lap times you must keep track of which racer completed each lap. Racers may “tag” their teammate in the pit area but the incoming racer must start at the same location as the exiting racer and pass the “baton.” Duo and team racers may race in whatever order they like (example: Racer 1 could do 2 consecutive laps, followed by Racer 2 who does 1 lap, followed by Racer 3 who does 3 consecutive laps).

Podiums

Prizes for the winner of each class, custom 6 Hours at the Mill medals for the top 3 finishers. Men and women open solo cash payout for Top 3.

Payout for open men and women is $150/$100/$50 for 5 or less registered racers and $200/$150/$100 if there are 6 or more registered racers in the category.

Podium presentations will begin at 4:00pm

The Non-Profits

These events are a partnership between JAMSQUAD Cycling and the Gunpowder United Mountain Bike Operators (GUMBO). Proceeds from the events will support three nonprofit groups: JAMSQUAD Cycling which provides refurbished bicycles for underserved youth and those in recovery and GUMBO whose mission is to develop and maintain a world class trail system at Gunpowder Falls State Park. A donation will also be made to the Friends of Jerusalem Mill. 

Parking

Parking will take place in the fields near the start/finish area. Racers may drop off items for their pit and then move their vehicle to the designated parking area. Please follow the directions of parking volunteers and use caution when crossing the road.

Partners

6 Hours at the Mill would not be possible without our amazing partners: Gunpowder Falls State Park, Friends of Jerusalem Mill, Independent Brewing Company, Bike Doctor of Bel Air, Kiddie Academy and Trek Bicycles.

Weather Policy

Gunpowder Falls State Park and the Friends of Jerusalem Mill generously allows us to race on these wonderful trails.  With their permission, the race will proceed if there is light rain. If there is heavy rain preceding the start or forecast for race day, the race will be postponed until Saturday, November 14, 2026. This race is a fundraiser (see above). In the event of inclement weather on both dates, the race will be cancelled. Please consider your registration fee a donation to the non-profit organizations.

Common Courtesy

Please be respectful of the environment and its inhabitants. We would like to remind everyone that we all have a responsibility to leave the race course cleaner than we find it on race day. All refuse should be discarded into appropriate containers. Any rider found illegally discarding objects in the park, the roads leading to and from the race course, and the on the race course itself will be dealt with accordingly. Trash containers will be available for rider’s to use around the property.
Sportsmanlike Conduct

The Race Promoters expect ALL spectators and riders to act like responsible adults. Use of profanity and blatant unsportsmanlike conduct will not be tolerated. This is a public park and family friendly event, so please be courteous to all volunteers and each other!

About Kids Bike League

Kids Bike League is a program of the nonprofit Georgia Hi-Lo Trail, Inc. Our mission is to empower Georgia’s next generation of leaders through off-road cycling by fostering outdoor exploration, environmental stewardship, self-confidence, teamwork, and community engagement. Learn more at KidsBikeLeague.org.

Kids Bike League is committed to our belief that every child deserves the opportunity to explore outdoors, discover their potential, and connect with their community through the joy of cycling. All children are welcome at Kids Bike League regardless of their family’s ability to pay. For information about scholarship opportunities, contact Kids Bike League Director of Programming, Alden Strandburg.

Understanding Bikes & Gear

Kids Bike League supplies bikes and helmets to participants who do not have access to their own bike. 

Participants are welcome to bring their own bikes. Bikes must be in safe working order (brakes functioning, tires inflated, handlebars and seat secure). Coaches can help inspect bikes and provide alternatives when bikes are unsafe.

All participants are required to wear helmets when riding. Participants are also encouraged to bring helmets if available. Kids Bike League will provide helmets for participants when needed.

Preparing to Join a Ride

What to Wear

  • Wear comfortable clothing, with socks and closed-toed shoes.

What to Bring

  • Squeeze water bottles will fit bottle cages affixed to our bikes.
  • Sunscreen and insect repellent are highly recommended.
  • Bring medications necessary for allergies or other potential medical emergencies (e.g. inhalers, epinephrine) .

Ride Dates & Locations

  • A complete list of ride dates and locations is available on KidsBikeLeague.org.

Close out your riding season with a ride to remember at Mohonk Preserve! 

LAST DAY TO REGISTER FOR 2026 GRIT IS MONDAY, 11/2. 

Join us for an epic fundraising ride across the Shawangunk Ridge, just 90 miles north of Manhattan. Pick from two distances 50.4 miles (4,711 ft. gain) or 23 miles (1,811 ft. gain). Both courses begin and end at the Ulster County Fairgrounds and once you enter the Preserve at mile two, the course is over 98% gravel on our famous network of historic carriage roads.  

This is not a race; think of it as a super challenging fun ride for a really good cause. Some of the gravel is rough and steep in spots. Expect some loose rock – especially on the descents. The long course includes an optional short technical section and a mandatory dismount/bike hike up a rustic steps near the “million dollar view.” Bring your gravel, cyclocross, or mountain bike. Class 1 e-bikes only are permitted if you can manage the technical sections. No road bikes, please.

You won’t be timed but you will be well-fed. Look for well-stocked aid stations with water, Skratch hydration and energy bars and bananas. A post ride party with food and music awaits you at the finish. Be sure to carry some food and water, and maybe extra clothes depending on the weather - this is a rain or shine event. You’ll be sharing the carriage roads with hikers and climbers, so bike bells are highly recommended. Be courteous to hikers and other riders when passing. Pack a spare tube, tools, and pump as there’s no mechanical support on course and no sag wagon. Helmets are required.

*Shout out to our friends at the Open Space Institute for granting us access to the River-to-Ridge Trail and to the Mohonk Mountain House who grant us special access to Sky Top and the golf course area for the event day only. Bikes are not allowed on carriage roads near Sky Top so you cannot pre-ride these sections of the course. No exceptions – If we blow this, access to Sky Top and the golf course will not continue. PLEASE DO NOT POST PICS FROM SKY TOP ON SOCIAL MEDIA PLATFORMS.

Also, near Spring Farm Trailhead, the private driveway near the Slingerland Pavilion, the Table Rocks Trail, and the Crag Trail on the Preserve are accessible to ride participants during the event only. You cannot pre-ride these sections.

Pricing (No price increase for 2026!)
50.4 Mile $150
23 Mile $125

Optional fundraising: (New!)
When you register you'll be set up with a fundraising page automatically. Raise $150 for Mohonk Preserve and we'll reward you with a super cool Grit pullover hoodie. Money raised will help us provide educational programs for children, maintain and repair the carriage roads you'll be riding on, conduct research and fight invasive species. 

Registration fees get you...

  • Pre-ride bike support on the morning of the event from Bicycle Depot staff
  • Bike plate
  • Grit sticker
  • Aid stations with, water, Skratch Labs hydration products and snacks
  • Finish line food, live music, beverages and beer.
  • A GRIT tech t-shirt.
  • A chance to win great prizes from our sponsors!
  • A gravel ride that's actually on gravel!
  • Satisfaction in knowing you're helping to raise money for a great cause!
  • Timed Strava segment for 50.4 mile course riders with prizes!


The Start
Expect a calm and controlled mass start for the 50.4 mile course at 8:30 am and the 23 mile course at 9:30 am. Riders will line up Goldilocks style: strong riders go to the front of the pack; moderate folks aim for the middle, and those planning a more leisurely pace, head to the back.

A pace car will lead riders for the first two miles of the course along public roads from Ulster Fairgrounds to Mohonk
Preserve property on Gatehouse Road.  Riders must remain in their lane behind the pace car. We mean it, calm and controlled.  

Once you’re off the public road and on the gravel, you can ride at your own pace.

*NEW Cutoff Time for 50-Mile Course*
Cutoff time for the 2026 ride is 2:00 pm at mile 31. If you don't think you can ride at this pace, we strongly encourage you to sign up for the 23 mile course. We want you back at the finish line in time for the the fun! Prize drawing will be at 3 pm. You need not be present to win, but we hope you'll be there! Note: The event takes place after daylight saving time ends so sunset is at 4:44 pm. 

Cancellation/Refund Policy:
Registration fees are non-refundable. You may wish to take the optional Registration Protection Plan from Allianz during registration. Shawangunk Grit is a major fundraiser for Mohonk Preserve. When you register, we hold a spot, make commitments to vendors, and deny others entry when the event sells out. Therefore, registration fees are non-refundable. We do allow transfers for a nominal fee. Event deferrals for any reason, including injury, are not allowed.

Should the event be canceled for a qualifying reason by the event producer such as adverse weather conditions which would make holding the event unsafe, your registration fees will deferred to the next year.

About Shawangunk Grit: 

The ridge where you’ll be riding is made from bedrock called Shawangunk Conglomerate, also known as Shawangunk Grit. Shawangunk Grit slabs were used to make millstones around the turn of the century and some of these millstones can still be seen on the land today. A nod to the history of the ridge is found in the Shawangunk Grit logo.

EventName: The 35th Annual West Hill Shop Cyclocross Race (RVCX Series #5)
EventNotes:
We are back for the 35th edition of the West Hill Shop Cyclocross Race. This year we are returning as a member of the River Valley Cyclocross Series! We are excited to host the final stop in the RVCX series and cannot wait to see you all in lovely SoVT. 

Racers will receive a discounted registration of $20 when they signup for a second race. This means no one has a reason to skip the single speed race.

DAY OF REG is offered for $50 CASH. See registration table for information.

The Venue: 

For one day per year, the grounds of the West Hill Shop and its neighbors is transformed into a race course! Space is at a premium, and we rely on multiple land owner's cooperation to put on the race. As such, please be respectful of the other land owners whose property we cross. (Green Mountain Spinnery, Farnum Insulators, The Putney Inn, and the residences on Brickyard Lane and Kathan Meadow Lane). 

Parking is located behind the Putney Inn (57 Putney Landing Rd, Putney, VT 05346), in the grass field marked in yellow on the map . Parking in the lot is reserved for guests of the Putney Inn. 

The Course:

The course will contain many of the classic features from past editions, like the fast, flowing woods section and the infamous run-up. As always, we try to keep it fresh so this year we've switched it up and have added a few new things. Expect to have to get off your bike and climb dry clay hills and pedal through a closed down paper mill. 

Course Layout:

 

Food: The Sweet Spot Cafe will be open on the day of the race, offering coffee, baked goods, and a variety of sandwiches. The Putney Food Co-op is also a short ride across the overpass with an extensive selection of grocery items, prepared foods, and sandwiches made to-order. 

Lodging: The Putney Inn is the most convenient option available! Affordable rates, preferred parking, right across from the course. We would not be able to put on the race without their support. 

There are plenty of AirBnBs in the area, and hotels in Brattleboro as well.  

Make it a weekend of racing by staying Saturday night, and attending Pumpkin Cross in Surry, NH on Sunday, November 8th! 

Getting There: 

From the South; Follow I-91 North to exit 4. Take the exit, and cross Putney Landing Road to enter the parking lot of the Putney Inn (57 Putney Landing Rd, Putney VT, 05346). Follow signs to the parking area behind the Inn.

From the North; Follow 1-91 South to exit 4. Take the exit, and turn right onto VT-5 North. Following signs to the West Hill Shop, turn right onto Putney Landing Rd (across from the Putney Food Co-op). After crossing the overpass, turn left to enter the Putney Inn  (57 Putney Landing Rd, Putney VT, 05346) parking lot. Follow signs to the parking area behind the Inn.

We are excited to see you for a great day of racing!

SafeSport

The PanAm Championships and DCCX organizing committee support the goals of SafeSport in protecting athletes and ensuring a positive environment for athletes, supporters and fans. 

Implementation of SafeSport protocols is the responsibility of the officiating crew. No person listed on the SafeSport Centralized Disciplinary Database is permitted in the pit area or team zones. Please provide the names of pit staff during check in (if different from staff you listed when registering). For non-U.S. support staff, a cycling federation license is required. Please present names of support staff and license numbers (if applicable) at registration. Specific questions about SafeSport guidelines pertaining to your support staff can be directed to the UCI or USA Cycling official in charge of pit pass allocation.

Licensing Requirements: All riders competing in the Pan American Championships, Masters Pan American Championships, and/or UCI C2 races must possess a current UCI International license.

If you currently do not hold a license of any kind the UCI license for an adult is $240.

If an athlete currently holds a USA Cycling domestic license, then you are able to purchase a UCI license add-on at a cost of $130 (the price difference between a USA Cycling license and the fee for a UCI license). You are eligible to purchase this add-on up to 30 days prior to an existing USA Cycling membership expiring. Per USA Cycling: this UCI license supersedes a domestic license and thus your domestic license will show as expired once the UCI license add-on is purchased.

The UCI/International license is valid for both UCI categorized races and any local/grassroots races.

More details available here: https://usacycling.org/get-started/bike-racing-for-adults

All riders in the DCCX amateur races must possess either a valid USAC license, a one-day USAC license or a UCI license with cyclocross coding. Non-US citizens must possess a valid UCI International license for insurance purposes. Non-US citizens from Canada can possess a Cycling Canada License.*

*If registering with a license from Canada is not an international (UCI) license, then applicable riders will be required to show proof of insurance that covers them while racing in the USA or sign a waiver acknowledging responsibility for all medical costs they may incur. USA Cycling's insurance does NOT cover riders with only valid domestic licenses from their respective national federation. Foreign federation UCI licenses are to carry with them proper medical insurance, but a Foreign Permission Letter (FPL) is required for it to be in effect. If no FPL is available, the rider is responsible for obtaining travel insurance that covers them while racing in the USA, and they accept full responsibility for medical expenses they incur. 

 

Racing age, per UCI 5.1.001:

The category to which the license holder belongs on December 31st, 2027, will be used for his or her participation in events for the whole season.

  • U23 and Elite Women will ride in the same event FOR UCI C2 EVENTS. NOT Pan Ams.
