  • Awards will be at the Start/Finish area after each event as soon as the final rider is in and results can be tabulated - usually within 30 minutes. This location may change, but you will be told in advance.

Main Venue: The hub of the event will be the Spring Lake Development District. (If you have ridden in Bike Sebring before, it is just off Hwy 98 on the original 100 mile loop near the end). Spring Lake is very excited to host our event this year. There is a nice clubhouse for registration and awards, plenty of room for parking, a large shelter for picnics and access to restrooms. The ONLY course will be the 3.66 mile loop within this residential subdivision. It has an excellent road surface, a bike lane on about 70% of it, low traffic, and a nice place for support to set up away from the houses. There are also bathrooms at the start-finish line that riders and crews will have easy access to.

Packet Pickup and on-site Registration:

At the Spring Lake Community Center: 209 Spring Lake Rd, Sebring, Fl 33876

  • Fri - Nov 13, 2026 - 4-7pm - Packet pickup and late registration (not required this year
  • Sat - Nov 14, 2026 - 5-6am-  Event day packet pickup and onsite registration. After 6am this registration will move to the start/finish line area at Echo Park.

The Events:

There will be 3 main events at 2026 Annual TT Championship (ATTC): 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour. All events are non-drafting Time Trial events.

Each event will have the following standard WUCA categories: gender, age-groups (8&U, 9-10, 11-12, 13-15, 16-17, 18-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80-84, etc as needed), all bike types (even fixed gear, velo, trike, recumbent, etc), solo as well as 2 thru 8 rider teams, Para-Cycling also welcomed in their own categories. There is something for everyone! High mileage in each category will be crowned the 2026 WUCA TT Champion for their selected categories. High Overall Mileage Male and Female for 24, 12, and 6-Hr will also be crowned WUCA Overall World Champion and will receive a free custom WUCA Jersey to commemorate the event.

Can I register for more than 1 event?

No - due to WUCA guidelines a rider can only register for a single Championship event.

What kind of bikes are allowed?

WUCA allows any type of Bicycle - anything with wheels actually, even 3 and 4 wheels, even ElliptiGOs. All types of upright bikes are also allowed, including a full TT bike setup - they are in the same Upright category. A Fixie has its own category. There are not any UCI rules regarding bike types in these Ultracycling races.

The Course:

The 3.66 mile loop is a wonderfully flat, smooth 3.66 mile loop that is Duane Palmer Blvd within Spring Lake. Everyone will ride CCW on this loop. The start-finish line for the whole event is located on this loop at the “Eco Park” entrance. 

Strava link: https://www.strava.com/routes/3165402422783783780

video of loop: https://youtu.be/r94cA1o3lrs 

Records at Spring Lake:

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vQRfHtLdbxIKWD5dvXnHwn2uikOxJj9AnWdT7Po419L_v33Lz2HIIXvYzQ18amuKv6dj1rQKRFR6OiJ/pubhtml

Food at the event:

I am working on a pre-race buffet at the local Spring Lake Golf Course restaurant - Since it is not Valentine's evening it should be possible this year, but I will keep you in the loop and you will be asked to state your preference when you register. The more early registrations and commitments to pre-event dinner we get the more likely we can have a private event like this within Spring Lake for everyone. I will also try and have an option for an awards supper for the 12-hour riders and their crew on Saturday evening and a nice breakfast buffet  for 24-hour riders and their crew on Sunday morning. All information about the meals will be emailed to everyone registered as it becomes solidified

Event protocol:

All events and riders will start and finish at the entrance to Echo Park on the north side of Duane Palmer Blvd. All riders should be ready to begin at 7am. RIders will be given a starting number based on their estimated avg speed and should line up in that order. This will prevent passing at the beginning of the event and allow good spacing between riders right from the start. A riders will be released every second or two. Don’t worry, your actual timer does not start until you cross the start-finish line.

A reminder that all events in this Time Trial Championship are non-drafting. All riders must honor the “non-drafting zone”. We have adopted the USA Triathlon (USAT) definition of this ‘zone’: as a “rectangular area seven 7 meters long (23 feet) and two 2 meters wide (6.5 feet) surrounding each bicycle”. This will provide a sufficient non-drafting area around each cyclist.

Due to staggered start times, each rider is highly encouraged to start their own timer on their GPS unit, phone, or personal stopwatch when they start, so they will know exactly when their event time has completed.

Each rider gets to acquire miles until the very end of their event time. This event is also aligning with the World Record setting standards within World UltraCycling Association (WUCA). This format allows all riders to ride until the very end of their timed event. No more of “If you can’t make it around the loop before the time expires - you are done”. Everyone will be encouraged and allowed to complete the current lap they are on until their time event expires. Your distance covered during your final partial lap will be prorated based on your final lap time.

Support crew Info:

Each rider is allowed to set up a single “support area” along the outside of Duane Palmer Blvd near Echo Park. All support must be set up on the outside of the loop since all cyclists will be riding CCW. This is to prevent riders from having to cross the road to get to their support crew.

 

Where to park your vehicle: (This is important for Safety)

  • The 24-hour cyclist(s) and their crew are permitted to park one of their vehicles of less than 25’ on the outside of the loop where their support is set up. This vehicle should be at least 10’ off the road. If the vehicle is more than 25’ or you have more than 1 vehicle these should be parked on the inside of the loop.
  • The 6-hr, 12-hr, and Century cyclists and their crew MUST park their vehicle on the inside of the loop. They still must set up their Pit area” on the outside of the loop - just their vehicle needs to be on the inside loop. This will make it safer and easier for them to leave CW (clockwise) after their event is done as there will still be many riders riding CCW (counter clockwise) on the loop for the remaining events.

NOTE: Do not set up near or in-between the existing houses which are mostly on the south and east sides of the loop.

The highlighted area in this map below shows acceptable locations to set-up for fixed rider support on the outside of the loop.. This is about a mile in length, so there should be plenty of room for everyone to set-up. Please limit yourself to about 35’ sections. More specifics below.

There will be a 50’ section on either side of the start-finish line that will be reserved for the Event Director and timing headquarters, and extra portable toilets - no support activities are allowed in this area.

There is no lighting or access to electricity on the 3.66 mile loop and in the start/finish area. It is strongly recommended that you bring these items:

  • A converter for your car to provide USB or 110V voltage from your car battery for your needs.
  • A small folding table or chair to be placed near the road with some identifying sign, image or “thing” that will help your rider identify their “spot”, and if your rider is in the 24-hour event, a light of some sort to illuminate it when it’s dark. Be creative so your rider has a great visual que.

Be sure to pull your vehicle off the road far enough so your rider can get off the road completely with their bike if they need to stop for aid. About 10’ should do.

Here is a visual to help you:

What to do if you have a mechanical need on the course:

If you or your cyclist has a mechanical issue on the 3.66 mile loop and needs your help, you have two options:

  • Go to them via your car or a bike (e-bikes are ok too) with tools and parts needed.
  • Go to the Event Director with your tools and parts and they will take you there or give you a vehicle to use (if available)

ALWAYS drive in the opposite direction of the riders for safety!

If the mechanical can be fixed (or the bike swapped out where the rider stopped, then they just start riding again. If they must return back to their Pit area for anything, they must return back to their original stopping place before continuing on.

Support of Riders:

The support crew is permitted to hand-off food and drink to their riders while the rider is moving. If the riders need to come to a full stop, they must be off the road so they do not interfere with any other rider.

Riders, when you are riding past all the support pit areas, you must ride the left side of your lane (near the center of the road) in this designated area so there is no conflict with those slowing down for handoffs or re-entering the road from a pit-stop.

Awards and souvenirs:

A Custom 2026 ATTC/Sebring t-shirt and Medallion is included in your registration fee. It will be given out during the award ceremony and will have your results printed on the back.

Custom 2026 ATTC/Sebring Jerseys and extra t-shirts & medallions for your crew can be ordered during the online registration. Deadline to pre order of Jerseys is Oct 1, 2026, and for t-shirts and Medallions it is Nov 1, 2026. I will order a few extra to sell during the event but I usually don’t have many.

An Awards and Recognition Ceremony will be held after each event. Everyone will be recognized for their achievement and have an opportunity for a photo with their medallion and crew. Special recognition will be provided for top overall place in each category.

Awards and recognition ceremonies will be held individually for each event as soon as the results for each event can be tabulated after completion.

  • 6-hr - Will be at the Golf Course Clubhouse with a buffet lunch available for pre-purchase
  • 12-hr - Will be at the Golf Course Clubhouse with a buffet dinner available for pre-purchase
  • 24-hr - Will be at the Golf Course Clubhouse with a buffet breakfast available for prep-purchase

Note: These may change as needed - but you will be notified when you complete your event.

Accommodations:

  • There is a huge variety of hotels, motels, and B&B’s available in and around Sebring within easy driving distance to Spring Lake. I suggest using some of the popular internet search engines for B&B's, home, and nightly lodging that are readily available.
  • I have also heard that the Kenilworth Hotel is going to re-open - I will update everyone if I see that happening.
  • I am also working with the golf course management company that controls lodging for many  golf course rentals in the subdivision. I will update this list or email that info out as I get it.
  • Camping is also available at the Highlands Hammock State Park, but not at the Spring Lake Community Center. 

Misc Info:

The 3.66 mile course will be surveyed for exact length, and all riders will be allowed to ride until their timed event expires, therefore allowing the greatest possible distance for each rider. There will be no mass start.

WUCA and GWR time and distance records on Surveyed Sebring courses:

Because of alignment with WUCA Record attempt rules, the 3.66 mile course has an official WUCA survey. This means this course can also be used to attempt any valid time and distance WUCA (and Guinness) record attempt. This attempt cannot however happen simultaneously with the Bike Sebring event. Contact records@ultracycling.com for more information about a WUCA record attempt.. Registration for this must be done at least 21 days prior to your record attempt to allow the pre-attempt documentation to be completed.

Many Thanks to Spring Lake Development District:

Lastly, we are very fortunate that the Spring Lake Development District has graciously allowed us to use their neighborhood for our event again. PLEASE be considerate of the homeowners and drivers you are sharing the road with. Keep off private property and keep noise to a minimum at all times. Use the time immediately after your event (while you are waiting for the award ceremony) to remove all personal items and all trash from your support area.

Please visit our website for venue information and racing requirements. https://www.utcx.net

UTCX is a USA Cycling-sanctioned series and follows USA Cycling’s Competition Category Policy.

Any UTCX category that is not designated as a Women’s or Junior category is open to all riders, regardless of sex assigned at birth. For the 2026 season, this gives riders 10 categories open to everyone, subject to the age and USA Cycling category requirements listed for each race.

Women’s categories follow USA Cycling’s eligibility requirements. Junior categories are based on age and sex category.

Our goal is simple: there is a place for everyone to race at UTCX, and all riders are welcome.

Your racing age is your age as of December 31, 2027 (this is cyclocross after all).

All fields will be scored separately.

First 2 rows of riders pre-registered by 8PM the day before the event will receive call-ups based on Cross Results rankings.  Riders will be separated into groups by start time within each wave.

Staging will begin 10 mins prior to each race.

In-person registration opens at 9:00 AM and closes 15 minutes before the start of each race.

Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leader.  Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and may not interfere with their progress.

Helmets are required for all riders on bicycles, even when not actively racing.  Radios, iPods, MP3 players, earphones, etc. are NOT allowed while racing.  

Please do not enter the course while a race is in progress.  The course official will announce when pre-riding of the course is allowed.  Riders entering the course for pre-riding must do so after the finish line and only after the "course is open' announcement has been made.  

Zip ties, limit screw mods, battery removal, and honor code pinky swearing for single-speed racers are allowed and encouraged.

Additional same-day races are $10 (free for Juniors 18 and under).  

The promoter and/or race officials reserve the right to modify, combine, or cancel races in the event of insufficient entries, dangerous weather conditions or other emergencies beyond their control.

No cash payouts for any heats.  In an effort to make the races more accessible and inclusive we are reducing entry fees to bare minimum required to cover race day costs!

EventNotes:
We Shred Rock Creek is back for 2026 – and it is shaping up to be one heck of a good time on bikes. Whether you’re looking to progress, try a new trail, ride Rock Creek (or any bike park!) for the first time, or just meet other rad women+ and girls who ride, this event is for you!

Women+ and Girls Take Over Rock Creek!

No matter your skill level, showing up and riding any mountain bike park can be a little intimidating, especially if you don't have a friend to ride with. That’s why we’re extending an invite out to women+ of all ages to join us at Rock Creek – without racing or egos – to have fun on the trails and progress at your own pace. Join pro downhill racer/ MTB skills coach/ mom Caroline Washam for a chill day of doing what we all love: riding bikes, talking about bikes, and relaxing a little too. (And yes, the park will be open to all men and boys, and we welcome all male supporters!) 

Highlights

  • $35 for Adult Passes (regularly $55), $32 for Youth (regularly $50). Register now to receive the discount code.
  • This is a FREE event; there is no fee outside of your discounted Ride Rock Creek pass!
  • It's a 90's Throwback Party! COSTUMES ARE ENCOURAGED! Bright colors, fun and a little tacky, grunge, whatever says “90's” to you, rock it!
  • FOOD TRUCKS – we will have food for purchase during the event!
  • Swag goodies from our sponsors!
  • EPIC Raffle!
  • PARTY LAPS with priority uplift access for women+!
  • *NEW for 2026*: RIDE WITH A COACH! Sign up to ride with a coach for an hour. Perfect if you've never been to Rock Creek or you'd like a guided lap down a trail that challenges you!
  • Pisgah Paparazzi (Stephanie Bush) will be taking photos!
  • Tasty beverages!

Itinerary

9:00am: Check in! Get your pass, grab some swag, sign up to ride with a coach.

9:50am: Welcome chat with Caroline! 

10:00am: Ride bikes! 

10:15-11:15am: Ride with a coach laps. Space is limited, sign ups open at 9:00am at check-in!

11:30am: PARTY LAP on Green River (green trail)! Priority uplifts for all women+

1:15-2:15pm: Ride with a coach laps. Space is limited, sign ups open at 12:15am at check-in!

2:30pm: PARTY LAP on Tumbleweed (blue trail)! Priority uplifts for all women+

3:30-4:30pm: HAPPY HOUR! Grab a drink, play some games, get social, chill out (or keep riding, of course)

4:30pm - EPIC RAFFLE! 

Things to Know

  • Can I buy my Ride Rock Creek pass at the event? 

You will receive your discount code in an automated email when you register for the event. Unfortunately, the discount code will not work when purchasing a pass on site. Please use the link provided in the email to purchase your pass before you arrive at the park. 

  • Should I register for the “First-timer” category?

One of the reasons We Shred exists is to help remove the barrier of entry for women+ and girls who have never ridden a bike park before. We want you to know that you are welcome at Ride Rock Creek and there are trails for you! This is your opportunity to try a bike park. Sign up for the “First-timer” category and receive a free bike park pass.

  • What if it rains?

This event is rain or shine! Check out the weather before the event and dress accordingly.

  • Can I ride my trail bike?

Yes! Enduro/ trail bikes or downhill bikes are acceptable at Rock Creek. We recommend riding a bike with at least 140mm of suspension travel and disc brakes that are in good working order! Rock Creek also has rentals, but make sure to reserve ahead of time: Rentals | Ride Rock Creek

  • What about protection?

Full-face helmets are required at Ride Rock Creek. You can rent a full-face helmet at Ride Rock Creek for just $10 (sizes Y, XC, S, M, L, XL, 2XL). Knee pads, elbow pads, gloves, chest protectors, and goggles are also not required, but recommended. 

  • Are there easy trails?

We never recommend downhill riding to brand-new riders. Being comfortable using your brakes, standing up and moving around on your bike is a requirement. However, Ride Rock Creek trails offer progression for all levels of riders. It’s not all massive drops, jumps and gnarly rock gardens! If you’re new, we recommend starting on the green trail, Green River, and working your way up to blue trails if you feel comfortable doing so.

  • Where should I stay?

Camping is available just down the road from the park at Rock Creek Campground. 

Cold Spring Basecamp is also right around the corner, and they offer camping as well as cabins and even a cool tree house!

Hotels, Airbnb/VRBO options are available in nearby cities, Hendersonville, NC and Travelers Rest, SC.

You can also find great resources for lodging here: 2024 National Championships | Ride Rock Creek

  • I’m still nervous - any advice?

Just come out! We'd love to meet you and chat! The event doesn’t cost anything just to be there and with the discounted pass, we encourage you to come out and give it a try. Start small, and we know you’ll love it.

  • More Answers to your Frequently Asked Questions can be found here: FAQs | Ride Rock Creek

Thank you for coming back for year three of our little shindig up in the Flint region; because of your participation (in the past 2 years) we've been able to give back roughly $2200 to Michigan based non-non-profits (LMB, Make-A-Wish)… That's rad.

Be mindful any tomfoolery or disrespect to any participant, official, volunteer, random wildlife, etc is grounds for dismissal from the race with limited opportunities for refund. Any race-day staff/volunteer remains the right to kick anyone out. Sorry Charlie. 

Again. Thank you for putting us on your ride calendar, and good luck!

Get ready for a unique South Texas cycling experience at the inaugural Old Coughran Town Gravel! Kickstand Racing is back as Kickstand Racing // STG2, and we are ready to debut a brand-new event on the Texas calendar. This race crosses the scenic backroads of Atascosa and Wilson counties. While map makers spelled the town Coughran, locals have proudly pronounced it "Korn" for generations. We are leaning into that insider heritage to bring you an authentic gravel experience.
This first-year event takes you deep into the heart of the historic region and across the legendary Eagle Ford Shale play. Don’t let the flat profile fool you. While you won’t find a lot of elevation on these routes, the relentless South Texas coastal winds can definitely make up for it—turning every open straightaway into a true test of grit. Whether you are hunting for cash prizes on the rugged unpaved backroads or simply riding for weekend bragging rights, come make history with us and tackle the finest caliche and wind that South Texas has to offer!

Traffic Control & Rider Responsibility

Your safety is our top priority, but gravel racing requires self-awareness on open public roads. Please note our official traffic protocols: 

  1. The First Right Corner (After the Start): A law enforcement officer will be stationed at the very first right turn after the start line to control traffic and safely launch each racing field onto the course.
  2. On the Course: Aside from the first right turn, all roads are open to public vehicular traffic. There are no corner marshals on the remote gravel sectors. Every participant is strictly responsible for navigating all intersections safely and obeying the bicycle traffic laws of the State of Texas (stopping at stop signs, riding predictably, and staying to the right).
  3. The Finish Line: Because the finish line is located at a three-corner intersection, a law enforcement officer will be stationed there to direct the occasional local traffic, ensuring every rider can safely sprint across the finish line. 

At the Finish Line

  • Cash Prizes and awards: for the top 3 overall Men and Women competing in The Iron Oak 68 fields.  45+ AG Recognition.  Purse pending class size.
  • Cash Prizes and awards: for the top 3 overall Men and Women in The Caliche Corridor 51.  Purse pending class size
  • Finish Line Refreshments and snack: post-ride cold drinks and snack foods waiting for all participants as soon as you cross the line.

  • Professional Chip Timing: Full timing services across all three routes so you can track your effort and compare times with friends after the ride. 

Route Links

  • The Iron Oak 68
  • The Caliche Corridor 51
  • The Leal Loop 31

Important Route Note: Iron Oak & Caliche Corridor (Mile 18.6)

At mile 18.6, County Road 139 ends at a T-intersection with CR 138. The route turns left.
  • Landowner Note: While this intersection may look like private property, it is a fully public county road. You are not trespassing. I have spoken directly with the gentleman whose property it looks like you are going through, and he is very nice.
  • What to Expect: Every time I have scouted this section, I have encountered a herd of goats and some birds. Enjoy the scenery, keep a steady pace, and stay on the main road!

The Noxturnal Ride is a one-night-only chance to ride Nox past sundown, while raising money for Valley Mountain Bikers.

This is a special event. Registration is limited to 175 riders. Online Registration closes November 12th at 11:59PM, or as soon as all available spaces fill up. There will be no day-of registration.
 

Dreading Daylight savings? The thought of less time to ride your bike got you down? Love riding Nox? Wish you could ride there at night? Now you can! Calling all spirits of the forest! Join the Valley Mountain Bikers in lighting up the night at Lake Nockamixon on Saturday, November 14th from 5 to 8 pm for the annual  “Noxturnal” night ride. 

 

VMB has obtained special permission from Lake Nockamixon State Park to host the unique one-night-only “Fun”draising event. In addition to rolling through one of our most beautifully maintained trail systems at night, your paid registration gets you: complimentary hot chocolate, s'mores, coffee, and some glowy bits to make your bike look extra special.  

What you Need: a properly functioning mountain bike, helmet, and at least one bike light—preferably one rated for trail riding (1000 lumen, 2 hour burn time recommended). Ebikes are welcome as long as they meet PADCNR e-bike policy ands standards.

Ride Routes: There are 3 distances options: 18 miles, 13 miles, and 7 miles. The longer distance riders will go off first, followed by middle distance, and short distance, 10 minutes apart to not overcrowd the trails. Follow the arrows and tape to make sure all riders are going in the same direction. If you are not familiar with the trails, we have an optional guided group ride (for the short distance only) that will leave last. Be sure to stop by the trail-side aid station for hot chocolate, coffee, and snacks! 

New for 2026: you can pre-order Noxturnal merch while registering for the event! Merchandise availability will be limited on the day of the event, so make sure you pre-order to get those sweet long sleeve shirts and hoodies! Youth sizes available, too! Deadline for pre-order: October 24th

Parking: All parking and event check-in will be at the Haycock Boat Launch off Rt 563 in Haycock Township. There will be no event parking at the Tower Rd Lot. Please follow parking instructions from volunteers when you ride. We encourage everyone to carpool to make sure everyone gets a parking space. 

Check-In: All riders must check in at the VMB tent in the Haycock Launch Parking Lot. Check-in will open at 4:00 p.m. Please plan to arrive and check in by 4:45 p.m.

Ride Departure Times:
18 mile ride: 5:00 p.m.
13 mile ride: 5:05 p.m.
7 mile ride: 5:10 p.m.

Guided 7 mile ride: 5:15 p.m.

Please, Be Cool! We have been given special permission by the State Park to hold this event. We must respect the trails, the park, and the rules we’ve been given. All riders must be off the trails by 9:00 p.m. Please respect instructions from rider leaders, sweeps, volunteers, and park staff. Leave no trace, and keep the trails and parking lots free of trash. 

Rain date: Sunday November 15th

EventNotes:
Cranksgiving York is food drive on two wheels to benefit The York County Food Bank! We're back at the Princess St. location!

Follow us on Facebook and Instagram for updates. A rider email will go out the week before and night before if you aren’t on socials.

There will be a taco bar at the 11AM Collusion Tap Works Side Show afterparty but you must preorder on Eventbrite.

All you need is a bike and a bag to carry the food! At registration, you will receive an itinerary that includes a map of the area, a list of grocery stores, and shopping list of food to purchase. This is not a race. You may leave after registration, as there is no mass start. You will plot your own route to as many of the stores as you'd like using the map provided, while buying the item/s on the list to bring back to the Princess St food bank by 11:15AM at the latest. Riders typically travel 10-15 miles and spend $30-35, however you may ride to as many stores as you'd like and purchase what you can afford, there is no minimum to participate. Participating riders should be comfortable riding on open city streets and in potentially heavy traffic and be prepared to carry the items purchased back to the Food Bank.

8:00 AM main event registration opens. 8:30 AM Wheels-up.

Turkey Bonus! For every turkey purchased you will get a drawing ticket for a special prize! The winner will be picked at the after party. No need to be present to win, just be sure to include your name and number on the ticket. 

Free Prizes: All riders will receive 1 drawing ticket for the prize table with registration. You will chose the drawing item you wish to be entered in before leaving on your ride and winners will be chosen before your return. Drawing prizes generously coordinated by BTI and donated by a number of generous bicycle industry partners. There's a possibility of prizes from PNX Bags, Ciclovation, KMC, Kenda, Black Ox, Orange Seal, Hiplok, Kryptonite, Fox, White Industries, Paul, Tubolito, Magura, PDW, Fox, and more!

Kind of a Race Drawing: In the spirit of an alley cat race, visit at least 8 stores and buy at least 2 items at each to be entered to win a prize that's a step above the general drawing prizes. You must be preregistered (no day of). Save your receipts to hand in when returning to the food bank by 11:15AM.

After Party at Collusion Tap Works Side Show: We'll be in the event space to the right of the main brewery. There will be a beef/chicken taco bar but you must purchase ahead of time here - Eventbrite Collusion Afterparty Food. Collusion’s regular kitchen also opens at noon but the food buzzers do not reach to the event space so you'll have to hang out over there until your food is ready. There will be 8 taps on in the event space.

 

FAMILY RIDE:

9:00 AM Registration opens.

The Family route will take you south on the beautiful Heritage Rail Trail toward Brillhart Station and return back to the Food Bank by 11:15 AM. Your grocery stop is at Lidl just off the trail on Richland Avenue where you may purchase any of the food on your list and also participate in the Turkey Bonus. Feel free to travel further south on the trail past Brillhart Station to The Howard Tunnel — you may even spot a steam train! This is the perfect ride for families and those that don't feel comfortable riding on open roads. Lidl is easily accessible by a dirt path right after crossing over Richland Ave.

If you'd like to make a monetary donation directly to the York Country Food Bank, please visit https://yorkfoodbank.org/donate/.

EventName: The Turkey Fry Road/MTB/Gravel Ride at Marty's Reliable Cycle
EventNotes:
The Turkey Fry Ride

@ Marty's Reliable Cycle of Randolph

 

This event is exclusive to MRC members and non riding family.  You will receive a password to register for event.  Please check the email that you used to register for Marty's Ride Club.  Passwords will be sent out a few times before the event.  

All registered participants please check your email on Friday Nov 13 for a Special Storewide Coupon.  This coupon can only be used at the Randolph location on Turkey Fry Ride Day.  

The fall is upon us! With the days getting shorter and colder you might need a little inspiration to get off the couch and on your bike. We have several supported and navigated routes to choose from. Choose your route and enjoy a fun road, MTB or gravel ride. 

After you complete your cycling adventure Darren "The Turkey Fry Guy" will be deep frying several turkeys for everyone to enjoy. 

We also wanted to give back to our community and help those in need. The Turkey Fry Ride will also be a Food Drive for the Interfaith Food Pantry. We'd like everyone who is coming on the ride to bring a bag of food for the food drive, $20 dollars cash or donate through the Bikereg page. Also, be sure to bring a side dish, beverages or dessert for the after ride festivities. There is no registration fee for the ride and is exclusive to MCC members.  Donations are suggested and not required to attend. 

 Please sign up early if your intend to ride so we can prepare. 

Please note: This is a bike ride and not a race. The roads are not marked. Your gps device is the best way to navigate the course.  You can also use the links below to print a map or cue sheet.

You

  • Bring food for food pantry or cash, check (Interfaith Food Pantry) donation
  • Bring side dishes, beverages and desserts
  • Register ahead of time so we know how many people are coming
  • Throw a chair in your car we have plenty of tables

Marty's 

  • Registration Check In Opens at 9:00 a.m. - Randolph Location. Please check in as soon as you arrive
  • Deep fry the turkeys
  • Provide routes to the self supported rides (located below)
  • Host the after ride festivities
  • Deliver donations to Interfaith Food Pantry the next day

 

You  might be asking what is the Interfaith Food Pantry? 

"The Interfaith Food Pantry is a community of neighbors helping neighbors, committed to ending hunger and supporting self sufficiency. Together we provide food, education and resources to inspire confidence and hope in the people we serve."

Here is a list of what types of food and items you can bring. http://mcifp.org/donate/donate-food/

Our freezer at the shop isn't very big, so please only bring non perishables or cash. 

We will donate the money to the Interfaith Food Pantry so they can fill in what they need. 

The 40 mile road and gravel rides start at 10am.   The 12 mile mountain bike ride starts at 10:15.  The 24 mile road ride starts at 10:30      All rides get back around the same time.   Turkeys will be ready by 1pm

Here are the Routes - Please upload them to your GPS device. Stop in the shop for help with uploading the routes.

     This 40 mile road route will have a three ride leaders with a 16, 17.5 and 19+ avg   Click Here for RWGPS Route

     

     This 27 mile gravel route will have one ride leader with a 13 avg speed   Click here for RWGPS Route

     

     This 12 mile mountain route will have a single ride leader 6-7 avg speed Click here for RWGPS Route

 

     This 24 mile road route will have a single ride leader 15-16mph avg speed Click Here for RWGPS Route

 

questions please email vic@martysreliable.com or call/text 973-945-2925

 

Parking - Marty's Reliable, Randolph Beach and limited spots at Marigold across from Marty's

EventNotes:
Join Velo Amis at Old Stone Cider for the Cider Stomper MTB Tour. Stay tuned to our Facebook for additional details and reminders and follow our Instagram @veloamis for bike-related content!

PLEASE CARPOOL! PLEASE CARPOOL! PLEASE CARPOOL! PARKING IS LIMITED! 

** REGISTRATION LIMITED TO 325 ADULT RIDERS. NO REFUNDS, PURCHASE BIKEREG INSURANCE. 
RAIN OR SHINE. WE WILL RE-ROUTE TO GRAVEL IF TRAILS WILL BE DAMAGED. 

** WE WILL HAVE AN 11:00am CUTOFF FOR RIDERS HEADING OUT TO WHITE CLAY CREEK ON THE LONG ROUTE. IF YOU DON'T MAKE THE CUTOFF, YOU WILL COMPLETE THE RIDE ON THE SHORT ROUTE. THIS RIDE WILL TAKE LONGER THAN YOU THINK! THERE IS A LOT OF SINGLE-TRACK. REMEMBER: IT GETS DARK AROUND 4:30pm. PLEASE DO NOT UNDERESTIMATE HOW LONG IT WILL TAKE YOU. YOU MAY WANT TO BRING LIGHTS. 

WE WILL PROVIDE RIDEWITHGPS ROUTES FOR BAIL OUT GRAVEL ROUTES BACK TO OLD STONE CIDER IF YOU NEED AN EASIER / FASTER ROUTE BACK. PLEASE BE AWARE OF HOW YOU ARE RIDING SO YOU CAN PLAN ACCORDINGLY. WE WILL BE OUT AND ABOUT, BUT DON'T COUNT ON GETTING PICKED UP. 

Last Call for drinks is 8:30pm and Old Stone closes at 9pm. Food trucks are on site until 7pm.  

REGISTRATION WILL OPEN AT 7:00am FOR THE LONG ROUTE AND 8:00am FOR THE SHORT ROUTE
LONG ROUTE MUST DEPART BY 8:30am and SHORT ROUTE MUST DEPART BY 9:30am 
LITTLE GOAT COFFEE ROASTERS WILL BE PROVIDING FREE COFFEE!
OLD STONE WILL OPEN FOR BUSINESS AT 11:00am

About the Ride: This is a mountain bike tour, with no competitive elements. The rides start and end at Old Stone Cider. A mountain bike is the bike of choice.  This is a RIDE, NOT A RACE.  

The long route (50 miles) is a four-park tour (Fair Hill, White Clay Creek, Redd Park and Middle Run) and the short route (26 miles) is in Fair Hill. Each route has a variety of surfaces. This is primarily a single-track event, however, there is also some double-track, road, field and gravel. The long route has FOUR rest stops (Mile 12, Mile 19, Mile 32 and Mile 42) and the short route has TWO rest stops at (Mile 12 and Mile 19).

After the ride, join us at Old Stone Cider. Each entry comes with an event drinking glass, a hard cider or beer (for cyclists 21 & up) or a non-alcoholic beverage, all you can eat french fries at the post-ride party, and rest stops along the route. Two food trucks will be on site for you to purchase food after the ride. Last call for drinks is 8:30pm and Old Stone closes at 9pm.  

Ride with GPS map files, cue sheets, and rider guides will be emailed to you after online registration closes. Routes will be marked, but you will be ultimately responsible to have the files and routes with you. Please note that the event director may alter the proposed routes due to acts of nature, road closures, or other things out of our control. We will contact you via email through bike reg so please read them. *Make sure that you add mail@BikeReg.com to your email safe sender list.  All rider communication is through BikeReg.

Registration & Pricing:

  • Entry Fee: $69 ($59 UNTIL 6/15/26)
  • Day-of Registration, if available: $80
  • Military/First Responder Fee $20: Please use the "Contact Event" link on BikeReg to learn how to receive your discount.
  • 19 Years Old & Younger Fee $20 - no late fees.

Registration Schedule
Sunday 11/15/26:
Long Route 50 MILE: Rider packet pickup and registration opens at 7:00am. All Long Route riders MUST depart Old Stone Cider by 8:30am.
Short Route 26 MILE: Rider packet pickup and registration opens at 8:00am. All Short Route riders MUST depart Old Stone Cider by 9:30am.

Until pre-registration closes, you are able to change the distance you registered for through your registration portal on BikeReg for FREE. If you realize you can't make the event, you may transfer your registration to another cyclist for just $5 through BikeReg as well, right until pre-registration closes.

Rules of the Ride:

  • Do not bring outside alcohol to the event.
  • Follow the rules of the road. Routes will be open to traffic. Please, NO headphones. The long route will ride on bike paths, so please ride single file and be courteous to other users. All routes are on heavily used bicycle and walking trails. Fair Hill Park is open to equestrians. Please talk to equestrians and ask how best to pass them. We want to be invited back, please be good stewards!
  • Sorry, NO REFUNDS. This is a rain or shine event and would only be cancelled if rider safety is at risk. If trails will be damaged, we will re-route the ride to gravel and hang out at Old Stone Cider!

Guy's Racing Club presents 

Pennypack on the Delaware CX (Permit #TBD)

 at

Pennypack Park
7801 State Road, Philadelphia, PA 19136

on Sunday, November 15th, 2026

This race is part of the PACX series!

Facebook: Like us on Facebook to receive updates and information about the race. www.facebook.com/WhirlybirdCross

Registration: Pre-reg closes Friday, November 13th at 5 PM.  Additional races for the day are a $10 registration fee.  Registration will cost an additional $10 on the day of the event, so please pre-register!  Late fees do not apply to juniors.  Day-of we accept cash or checks -- no plastic.

Registration/Sign-in and race number pick up opens on-site at 7:30 AM and closes 30 minutes before each race.

No refunds will be given with the exception of circumstances that fall within those described in "Race Cancellation Policy," below.

Licensing: USAC permit #TBD.  All racers (except for the kids race) must present a valid license at registration and sign a USAC event release form. Smart phone license verification will be accepted; download the USAC app for better viewing.

  • Beginner One-Days One-Day licenses for beginner categories are $15 and may be purchased on USA Cycling’s website, or on-site at the event.
  • Experienced One-Days If your categories prohibit you from entering a race with a beginner one-day license (anything but cat 5), you can purchase the experienced one-day license for $35. The experienced one-day license is only available on USA Cycling’s website.

USAC annual license renewals will be available on USA Cycling's website or at the race.

Your cross racing age is your age as of December 31, 2027 (not 2026!).
 
Racers under 18 (real age, not racing age) must also have a parent sign the release form (can bring one pre-printed from the USAC site and signed by the parent if the parent cannot attend the race). Kids racers also need a parent signed release form.

The Venue: 

Location: Pennypack Park, 7801 State Road, Phila., PA 19136

Pre-riding:  NO PRE-RIDING IN THE PARK PRIOR TO RACE DAY

Equipment: Mountain bikes are allowed as long as they do not have bar ends. No aero bars are allowed.

Clothing: Helmets are required for all riders on bicycles, even when not actively racing (eg, while riding from the parking lot). Per USAC regulations, racers must wear a jersey with sleeves covering the shoulders. No tank tops are allowed. Race radios and earphones for playback (eg, mp3 player) are not allowed while racing.

Staging: All racers should present to the start grid 15 minutes prior to the start of their race. 

Call up Protocol: The call-up protocol will be based on Race Predictor rankings as posted on Crossresults.com, followed by order of pre-registration. ALL CALL-UPS WILL BE BASED ON PRE-REGISTRATION. DAY-OF REGISTRATIONS WILL START AT THE BACK OF THE FIELD. Call-up protocol for the Cat 4/5 Men and 9-14 Men and Women will be based on order of registration. Bib number will indicate your start grid position. NOTE: IF YOU ARE RANKED, BUT DO NOT PRE-REGISTER, YOU FORFEIT YOUR CALL-UP PLACEMENT AND WILL BE PLACED ON THE START GRID BEHIND THE LAST PRE-REGISTERED RACERS.

FOR YOUR BEST POSITION ON THE GRID, PRE-REGISTER!

Lapped riders: Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leader. Riders being passed must yield and not interfere with the progress of passing riders. The officials will provide any necessary additional instructions prior to the start (such as whether or not riders will be pulled from the race prior to the end).

Results: The first three finishers of each race should report to the podium immediately after the race for podium photos.  The protest period starts at posting and lasts 15 minutes. It is the rider's responsibility to have all errors corrected during the protest period. After results are final awards will be available at registration.
 

Kids Race: A fun kids race will start at 12:30 pm for kids too young to race on the real course. A parent must sign the event release form prior to the race, and each kid will be given a race number. Pedal bikes or strider bikes are acceptable. All entrants will receive prizes for participation.

Food: TBD

Restrooms: TBD


Race Cancellation Policy:  If weather conditions are such that the race would cause significant damage to the property, e.g., heavy rains and water drenched grounds prior to and during the event, the race may be canceled. The race promoter will make every attempt to determine prior to race day if the race needs to be canceled, however, under extreme conditions part or all of the races may need to be canceled on the day of the race. Every effort will be made to hold the race, including making course modifications if necessary. If the race is canceled on the day prior to the race, notification will be sent to all pre-registered racers via email, and via the race's Facebook page. EventNotes:
(Early bird pricing of $40/Adult and $160/Adult Series increases 

to $45/$185 on 9/15/26 at midnight)

Our grand finale for the Rust Belt Ruckus CX Race Series comes back to One O Four Farm. This course is so good we race it twice!  Jon and Shannon always change things up so the course feels new and fresh even if you've raced it (every single time) like I have… It's rolling, has perfectly apexed turns through orchards and farm fields like flying through a labyrinth, and some punchy techy parts back by the beaver sanctuary. It really doesn't get much more fun than this for a cyclocross course.

Non Sanctioned, no USAC license required

All competitive racers need an approved helmet

Participants under 18 years of age are required to have a signed parental consent form.

NO PARKING ON ROAD (Rt. 104)

Please see confirmation email for exact event location and parking instructions.

Racing will start at 10:30am with a course designed specifically for our Junior racers and continue through our final race of the day ending at or around 2pm. 

We will allow day of registration but ask you to please pre-register if possible. These events take many volunteers to run successfully and any and all preparation that can be done ahead of time makes these days run much smoother. Double up and race a second race for only $15! 

Back for 2026: The Buffalo cyclocross promotors have teamed up with The Campus Cycling Collective (the organizer of this race) to bring you The Rust Belt Ruckus! : A Buffalo Cyclocross Series This will be race 3 of 5 in the series. If you'd like to register for the full series to save a few bucks and get all your registrations done in one shot, please go HERE! (Registration for series closes 10/9/26)

EventName: Rust Belt Ruckus 2026 - A Buffalo Cyclocross Series
EventNotes:
The Campus Cycling Collective, Inc. is proud to present The Rust Belt Ruckus! — A Buffalo Cyclocross Series

***Early bird pricing now until 9/15/2026 at midnight***

Adult Race Entry $40 -> $45 (after 9/15)

Adult 5 Race Series Entry $160  -> $185 (after 9/15)

Register early and save some hand up money!

**There will be day of reg at every event (cash only and $10 extra)**

*Individual Race Registrations are linked below*

Junior and U19 racers are encouraged to apply for our new limited

CCC Race Fee Scholarship : Fill Out This Form!

Overview

Back for 2026 your Buffalo cyclocross promoters have joined forces with the Campus Cycling Collective to bring you a better cyclocross season. The Rust Belt Ruckus will consist of a 5 race series in a condensed season format going from October 11th to November 15th. (no more August 80 degree cross race followed by weeks of no local races) All races will be UNSANCTIONED, meaning you do not need a USAC license to participate, or worry about one day licenses. This removes barriers of entry for Canadians, former license holders who miss riding in the tape, and new racers. 

We will have consistent race schedules and a condensed “Siuta” format so the entire day fits into 3 ½ hours of racing. This will put more people on the course at once making it more fun, not a solo time trial. This also gets you back to your family or allows plenty of hang out time or to help set/clean up the course. 

Each race will have its own podiums and awards, but at the final race on November 15th at One O Four Farm's Gobble OOF CX, we will present series awards for those who participated and performed the most & best & worst,  along with some other CX Promoter picked superlatives…. You must complete 4 races to be included in series awards/results.

Event Schedule

The Rust Belt Ruckus consists of 5 independent cross races. The races take place in October and November across the WNY region. You may sign up for the entire 5 race series on this page (and save $40!). Or you can sign up for individual races using the links below.

  • 10/11/26 - Knox Farm CX (East Aurora) Race One
  • 10/25/26 - OOFF CX (Lockport) Race Two
  • 11/1/26 - Beaver CX (Grand Island) Race Three
  • 11/8/26 - JR West Falls CX (West Falls) Race Four
  • 11/15/26 - Gobble OOF CX (Lockport) Race Five & Series Finale

Adults race all 5 races for $160 (plus fees). For juniors it's only $60 (plus fees) 

These are the early bird fees. After 9/15/26 Adults registration increases to $185. 

You can add a second race at EVERY race for an extra $60 ($15x4 one free).

 

Race Day Schedule

  • 9:30 am Registration Opens
  • 10:30 am Race One: Juniors u15 (on a shortened course)
  • 11:30 am Race Two: Cat 4/5, SS, Women Open, Women 4/5
  • 1:00 pm Race Three: Open 1/2/3/4/5, Cat ¾ Men 1:15 pm: Masters 40+, 50+, 60+, 70+
  • Race Podiums will be done after each race.
  • At Race 5 / Series Finale, all podiums will be done at the end. This includes race and series level podiums.

Series Rules

The series consists of 5 races, but only 4 results are required for overall series rankings. We don't want a single mechanical to ruin your overall ranking. 

4 results required to be eligible for series rankings and awards. 

If you complete all 5 races, the worst result will be discarded.

 

If you sign up for the whole series you only need to register ONCE (on this page).  You will receive a discount that equates to ONE FREE RACE. And you will SUPPORT all of us Buffalo cyclocross promoters who stick our necks out & volunteer our time. All with an end goal of getting to rode around a field like we are all 12 years old, with you, having the time of our lives…

 

So, what are you waiting for? Sign up today and help us Bring The M*utha F*cking R*ckus!

EventNotes:
(See Englisg Below)
La Buckland, un événement épique de vélo de gravelle, se déroule au cœur des Appalaches du Québec, offrant aux participants un défi inoubliable. Le parcours, exigeant et pittoresque, se caractérise par son dénivelé positif. Le Gros Buck affiche plus de 3000 mètres sur une distance de 146 kilomètres, tandis que le Petit Buck présente environ 2000 mètres sur une distance de 100 kilomètres. 

Vous vous demandez à quelle distance vous inscrire? Vous pouvez changer d'idée à l'intersection du Petit et Gros Buck (km 75). Vous souhaitez relever le défi du Gros ou opter pour le Petit si vous préférez revenir à la bière plus rapidement. 

En 2025, nous introduirons une nouvelle distance de 50 km, plus accessible, conçue pour permettre aux participants de découvrir la région et le charme de Buckland à travers les parcours de gravelle. Il est è noter qu'il n'est pas possible de changer d'épreuve lorsque vous participez au 50km. 

Vous aurez la chance de parcourir des secteurs à couper le souffle, chacun aussi unique que l'autre : traverser la majestueuse forêt du Parc du Massif du Sud, explorer les secteurs des éoliennes avec leurs vues panoramiques, et suivre les paisibles rangs qui traversent les champs pittoresques de la région.


-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
La Buckland, an epic gravel bike event, takes place in the heart of the Quebec Appalachians, offering an unforgettable challenge. The course, demanding and picturesque, is characterized by its positive elevation gain. “Le Gros Buck” boasts over 3000 meters over a distance of 146  kilometers, while “Le Petit Buck” features approximately 2000 meters over a distance of 100 kilometers. 

Wondering which distance to register for? You can decide at the intersection of the “Gros Buck” and the “Petit Buck”. Do you want to take on the challenge of going longer or shorter and prefer to get back to the beer more quickly? 

In 2025, we are introducing a new, more accessible 50 km distance designed to allow participants to explore the region and the charm of Buckland through gravel routes.

You'll have the chance to explore breathtaking sectors, each as unique as the other: traverse the majestic forest of Parc du Massif du Sud, explore the wind farm areas with their panoramic views, and follow the peaceful country lanes that cut across the picturesque fields of the region.

General Cedar Blitz Rules/Info:

Use your age at the end of the year, Dec 31st, 2027 for category selection.

Race will take place rain, snow, sleet or shine... In the event of severe weather such as thunderstorm, lightening,  blizzard, hail, we will postpone the race until conditions improve. Seek shelter if severe weather occurs before, during or after the event.  If severe weather causes the event to be cancelled, we will not be able to postpone this event to a later date. Determination and definition of adverse, inclement, or severe weather conditions will solely belong to the discretion of the Race Director.

This is NOT a closed course race.  This race is open to vehicle traffic.  Obey All traffic laws.  You must follow the Michigan Vehicle code.  Cycling road rules apply.  You must STOP at all stop signs, always yield to the right-away.  Do NOT cross the center-line of the road.  Ride No more than 2 abreast.  Violators will be disqualified.

Minimum 10 racers per category.  Race categories that do not meet minimum amount of racers may be combined with another category at the race directors discretion.

ANSI/Snell approved bicycle helmets are required.  No earbuds allowed.  Your bike must be in good working condition.
Time limit of 4 hours for 18, 36, and 50 mile racers.  It will be implemented and at the discretion of the race marshals and Race director.  Time limit of 10 hours for the 124 mile race (14 mph average).

THERE ARE NO REFUNDS.  THERE ARE NO DEFERMENTS.

Additional Rules/Info for 124 Mile Course only: Start time is 6am, July 10th.  14 mph average is expected. Cut off time 4pm.  This is an Unsupported course.  There are No course marshals, and the course is unmarked.

  • GPS computer with course download is mandatory
  • Lights are mandatory
  • This is an open course.  You must obey all traffic rules.
  • Must provide your own support or transportation if you do not or cannot finish.
  • Aid station with bag drop available.  Racers can pick up their bag after awards.  No other aid is allowed.

EventNotes:
About The Race + Ride

Presented by the Adirondack Foothills Cycling Club (AFCC), the North Winds Gravel Classic will host hundreds of riders from all over the country as they traverse the challenging and scenic dirt roads of the Tug Hill.   


The NWGC offers two course distances (65 and 38 miles) featuring the Fastest Gravel in the Northeast. The routes offer fast hard racing for traditional elite and masters racers and exciting challenges for recreational riders and new cyclists alike.

 

Following the races, all riders are invited to celebrate at our after party featuring music, food, and the region's finest craft beverages.

 

About The Courses

All courses begin near Tuggers Grill, Bar and Campground and wind through some of upstate New York's most remote wilderness, beautiful gravel roads and scenic mixed surface roads; All along the route catching glimpses of Maple Ridge Wind Farm.

 

65 Mile Course 

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/55486242

38 Mile Course

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/55146998

 

About The Tug Hill

The Tug Hill region lies between Lake Ontario and the Adirondacks. Larger than Delaware or Rhode Island, its 2,100 square miles comprise one of the most rural and remote sections of New York State and the Northeast. A scattering of public lands covers a tenth of the region, with most of that land used extensively for timber production, hunting, and recreation. The rest is privately owned forest, farms, and homes, all of it working land that supports the region’s way of life.  Tug Hill’s total population is just over 100,000, with two-thirds of those people concentrated in villages around its edge. Its densely forested core of about 275 square miles is among New York’s most remote areas, with a population of just a few thousand and few public roads.

 

Race Rules

Violations of any of the rules below could lead to being DQed! Promoter reserves the right to shift start times, change course layout, and combine fields based on safety issues and field sizes. Be sure to check your pre-race email for all final details before race day.

 

  • All riders must wear a helmet

  • All courses are open to traffic so follow the rules of the road.

  • Do not litter on course.

  • Be kind to everyone: Course marshals, volunteers, other racers, spectators, locals etc. A lot of people work hard to put this together, help us continue it by being kind.

  • You can race any bike you want (as long as it’s not an e-bike) but we recommend a gravel, mtb or cross bike. Road bikes are not advised.

  • No e-bikes in the competitive field. 

  • The majority of gravel is pristine and very fast with only a handful of sections with some big stones.  We recommend a minimum tire width of 35mm.

3: Please allow us up to 48 hrs to review your application, if accepted you will be emailed a password to access registration on this page. (Past participants are already qualified for camp.  If you have never done camp before, we will review the application and may follow up if we have any questions for you.)

4: We will email the registration link and password for you to register for the camp(s) of your choice and fill out the required camp waivers.

Camp Road / Gravel June 14-19 https://www.bikereg.com/mh-road

Camp MTB 1 June 21-26 https://www.bikereg.com/mh-MTB-1

Camp MTB 2 June 28-July 3https://www.bikereg.com/mh-MTB-2

Camp MTB 3 July 19-24 https://www.bikereg.com/mh-MTB-3

5: Ride a lot and get ready for this summer! We will email you a packing list and other forms a few weeks before camp.

 

What is Mars Hill Cycling Mountain Bike Camp

We are a 6-day overnight camp for intermediate to advanced male and female junior riders looking to develop skills, confidence, and fitness. Each day introduces new skills with opportunity to practice on easy terrain before putting them to use out on the trails. We'll get in plenty of mileage and keep the stoke level high by riding some of the best trails Western North Carolina has to offer, including Pisgah National Forest and Dupont State Forest.

What you can expect: skills-based instruction adjusted to your skill level for technical descending, climbing (we earn our turns!), cornering and braking; safety and situational awareness on trail; equipment selection, maintenance and repair; training and racing strategies; proper bike fit, fueling, and recovery; lots of fun group dynamics. Plus picnics, games, movie nights and waterfalls

 

Paying for camp:
1 The most direct: You can follow the instructions above and register on Bike-Reg.  This is the most direct way.
2 The least expensive: You can pay via check, which avoids Bike-Reg transaction fees ($70), after paying we will email you a code to complete your registration on Bike-Reg. 

 

Mars Hill Cycling Camps and USA Cycling: 

For years Mars Hill Cycling Camps have aimed to provide not only a fun and enriching summer road and mountain bike overnight camp experience, but also to provide education and training to help campers reach the next level in their sport.  For 2023 and 2024 we were  recognized by USA Cycling as a part of their Athlete Development Pathway Regional Camp system.  For 2025 there are no longer USAC ADP Regional camps, but Mars Hill Cycling Camp aims to continue building on the years of success we have had with that model, including offering certified rider instruction, challenging riders' fitness, building character and helping riders find their next opportunity in sport. All campers can expect the same riding, fun, and enrichment we’ve always provided.

 

    Education: Discussions and seminars on multiple topics to improve athletic performance.

    Skills: Sessions designed to increase understanding of skills and foster safe methods for improvement.

    Training: Solid training and testing protocols to increase fitness.

 

Exceeding Industry Standards: 

Mars Hill Cycling Camp also aims to meet or exceed relevant industry standards including certified coaching staff with PMBIA and USA Cycling Coaching Licenses, Safe Sport Training Staff, First Aid and CPR Trained Staff, Wilderness First Aid Certifications, insured and permitted to operate.

 

Housing: 

The default dorm housing is dual occupancy. Community bathrooms, separate wings for men and women. We will pair you with a sibling, a friend that you know, or with a camper of similar age.  This works great for most campers but we also understand that some campers may have a need for a single occupancy dorm.  A single occupancy room can be added for $150 via BikeReg or at check in on a first come first serve basis.

 

For more information about camp please see our website https://www.marshillcyclingcamp.com/mountain-bike-camp. 

We also have a facebook where we post daily recaps https://www.facebook.com/MarsHillCyclingCamp/ and an instagram https://www.instagram.com/marshillcyclingcamp/

If you cannot pay for camp at one time, we do allow installment payments. We also allow a non-refundable deposit to be made to hold a space in camp.  Email reid@marshillcyclingcamp.com or hugh@marshillcyclingcamp.com if needed.

Refunds

Tour Da Yoop, Eh does not offer direct refunds. If there’s any chance you might not attend, buy the registration refund insurance during sign-up. Allianz also offers trip insurance that takes just minutes to purchase online. It can even cover additional costs like travel and lodging, and it can be purchased after you register.

Ride Details

The ride starts and ends in Manistique, taking a clockwise tour around the Upper Peninsula. It covers 1,200 miles total, with each day averaging about 120 miles. Slower riders roll out at 7:00 AM, followed by faster riders at 8:00 AM from each town’s host hotel. Riders form groups based on their pace and follow mapped routes along quiet roads to the next host city.

We handle the logistics. TDY transports your luggage from hotel to hotel, provides water stops every 30–40 miles, and has SAG vehicles and support cars tracking riders throughout the day. The U.P.’s narrow shape also makes it simple to get back to your car if you’re only riding part of the tour. Taxi services are available as well. Find more details under the Rider Central tab at https://www.tourdayoopeh.com.

Registration

Registration is simple. Choose how many days you want to ride and which sections you’ll join. You can adjust your schedule later if needed, and if you start with five days but decide you want the full ten, you can add days anytime.

Jerseys

Returning riders who already own an orange camo jersey can indicate that during registration to receive a reduced fee. New riders will have the jersey cost included in their registration. When you complete your final section, you’ll earn a free plaid jersey and a spot in the Hall of Plaid (https://www.chasingplaid.com) to celebrate your accomplishment.

Crooked Gravel takes a few cues from an exploratory event the legendary Ron Kiefel put together a decade ago called Crooked Roubaix. Back before gravel bikes were really a thing, Kiefel and some friends set out on a 95-mile dirt-road adventure from Winter Park up into the high mountains on road bikes. Fast forward to 2027 and we’ve all become part of the exciting world of gravel.

Winter Park, Colorado has hundreds of miles of smooth and stunning gravel roads featuring beautiful wildflowers, Aspen groves and babbling brooks.

The Rambler course packs a perfect punch — 25 miles of rolling terrain, flowing gravel, and wide-open mountain views before looping back into town. Fast, fun, and scenic, it’s the ideal mix of challenge and reward.

Looking for more? The Grinder course turns things up a notch — more miles, more climbing, and even bigger views. You’ll top out at 10,500 feet after a 12-mile, sustained climb that will test your legs and fill your lungs with that high-country air. It’s tough, wild, and absolutely unforgettable.

Want the most? The new Epic course combines the other two courses into one giant course!

New for 2027! Three courses, 25 mile - Rambler, 67 mile - Grinder or the new 93 mile - Epic course of pure Colorado challenge — climbs, views, and grit at 10,500 feet. How far will you go? Push your limits on Colorado’s most scenic and challenging gravel routes. 

If nothing worth doing is easy, then Crooked Gravel is definitely worth doing!

Course Description 

In mid-summer, the High Country of North Carolina enjoys 80-degree temperatures while the surrounding East Coast temperatures hover in the high 90s. Early August is a prime time to be in Boone. 

After a short downhill and a climb up the gorgeous Shull's Mill road, the course passes the Blue Ridge Parkway and turns onto Hwy 221. This section of road was hand built in the 1890’s across Grandfather Mountain and served as the Blue Ridge Parkway until the 1980’s. This second timed section is like a paved roller coaster. 

After passing the Grandfather Park entrance, the downhill into Linville is a local favorite stretch of road. The route passes through the Avery County seat, the town of Newland. The back roads of Cow Camp and Squirrel Creek lead to the North Toe River Valley.  Here, riders enjoy a few tranquil moments in the valley before the ascent, and third timed section, on the back of Beech Mountain.  

Another nice downhill waits on the other side. The beautiful Bethel Valley brings riders to a climb to the Tennessee State Line to end the forth timed section.  From here, the route cruises on a very long gradual downhill grade through the valley and communities of Sugar Grove and Valle Crucis before it takes a climb up Laurel Fork and White Oak roads back to the town of Boone.

The Old Fort Fifty will be held on the rugged, legendary trails that have made the area famous in the mountain bike world while also incorporating some newer trails recently built by the G5 Trail Collective.  While the 30.9 mile distance is on the shorter side for an endurance race, don't fool yourself into thinking this is going to be a walk in the park.  You will be served up a heaping helping of elevation gain, climbing 4874 feet and descending an equal amount over fast and technical chunky terrain as well as some super omega flow. There will be two rest areas along the way (Mile 13 and 23.5) stocked with plenty of water and snacks.

The Old Fort Fifty will be open to cyclists AND runners!

 

Starting and finishing at Camp Grier, racers will first head over to the Gateway Trail System, an incredibly well-built network of modern, flow-heavy trails.  From there, you’ll head up and over to the raw goodness of Star Gap and its infamous Heckle Rock.  Finally, you’ll have a couple “gotta get up to get down” climbs before being rewarded with descents down both Bernard Mountain and the ear-to-ear grin-inducing Kitsuma Trail.

 

There will be plenty of affordable indoor lodging and camping options at Camp Grier the night before and also after the event with plenty of room for the family to make a weekend out of it.  You can stay Friday night and wake up close to the start line, and if you decide to hang out Saturday night, you can race or spectate the Pisgah Enduro on Sunday!  During your stay, you’ll have access to the lake, showers, a post-race cookout, and refreshments provided!

 

Both the Old Fort Fifty and the Pisgah Enduro will be part of the King of Pisgah Series.

EventName: THE BRECK EPIC MTB STAGE RACE
EventNotes:
THE 2027 BRECK EPIC
 

August 15-20, 2027
Back to the beginning. When mountain biking was a about big rides with friends. About lending a hand when a rider went down. About how a shared experience on a challenging backcountry course disproportionately enriched all involved.

INCREDIBLE COURSES
The Breck Epic is composed of 6 BIG backcountry loops (3 loops for the 3-day Epic-curious events), each between 35 and 50 miles long. The event is unique in that it employs a cloverleaf format; each loop starting and finishing within a mile from downtown Breckenridge. The race utilizes the magnificently sprawling and interconnected network of trails that span the width and breadth of Summit and Park Counties. 

When mapping out the courses we asked ourselves; “What big rides would we want to tackle if we had most of the day to slaughter and 6 of our best friends along for the ride?” The answer lies before you. The six stages that compose the Epic are a well-rounded rider’s dream. Long middle-ring climbs, endless big-ring mashing descents.

THE LONG HAUL
The 2027 version of the Epic marks our 19th edition. That's a lonnnnng time! "Time," some would.say, "To spice things up!" We think you'll like what we have on deck. The race is rad. The courses are beyond fun. The vibe? Mid-90’s mayhem. And Breck? It's amazing. Great people, amazing food and unbelievable weather.

In an average year, Epic will host riders from 25 different countries and 40 states. Why? We think because events like ours are just rare. It's a unique combination of mayhem and organization, with a huge emphasis on camaraderie and community.

BIGGER ISN'T BETTER - 400 RIDER LIMIT
We'll also be limiting the field in 2027. This is a statement about how we feel about the quality of the race experience. We simply believe that it's more fun when there are fewer people out there. Bigger isn't better. BETTER is better. We think you'll have a better time without your snout poking up some other rider's tailpipe all day. Not that there's anything wrong with that. But as they say, unless you're the lead dog, that view is always the same.

We feel that our course can handle more, but the question is, "Should it?" Our personal answer is no. Our commitment to our riders and to our trail network and community is to keep our numbers down. Because it's a better experience for our riders and because it lessens the impact on our trail system.

So yeah. Space is limited. That's by design.

If a weeklong tour of the world's greatest high alpine trail network sounds like your cup of tea, come join us. We’ve got great people in a great town with courses that you’re gonna need to ride to believe. What else do you really need?

MikeMac

High-speed East Coast technical rocky rooty singletrack ENDURO racing in Pisgah National Forest, around Old Fort, along the steep escarpment of the Blue Ridge Mountains. With dizzying vertical descents to quad-crushing climbs, you will ride a roller coaster that puts this region on the map for the downhill minded. The venue is an actual Summer Camp. There’s a lake, pump track, post-race cookout, and more!  Choose bunkhouse or car/tent camping and spend the weekend racing and enjoying life!

The course starts in the shadow of the highest peak East of the Mississippi, Mount Mitchell, on the legendary Heartbreak Ridge trail. Stage one and two drop over 3000' elevation in a combined 4.5 miles. Stage three follows with the most amazing trail that parallels Interstate 40… Kitsuma, and descends another 1300' in 2.5 miles to the finish. Start/Finish and lodging at Camp Grier in Old Fort, NC (where the after-race party will be waiting for you).

The Pisgah Enduro will be a SUNDAY (one-day only) event. If you would like a full-weekend of racing and camping at Camp Grier join us for the Old Fort 50 being held on Saturday!

If you are craving more challenges, be sure to register for the entire King and Queen of Pisgah series!

FAQ's

1. Am I registered?
     – Please check your inbox and spam folder for a confirmation email from BikeReg.com. If you did not receive a confirmation email please contact the race director at pisgahpro@gmail.com.

2. Are we using timing chips?
     – YES! We will be using a fly-by chip timing system. This means the timing system will record your time automatically as you cross the start and finish lines of each stage.

3. Will there be drinking water on course?
     – YES! There will be an aid station between stages two and three. The aid station will have water, first aid, and snacks. 

4. How does the start work?
    
     – All racers will pedal from Camp Grier to the top of Heartbreak Ridge trail using Heartbreak Ridge trail. This includes five miles of pavement followed by a five mile, 3000' elevation gain, single track climb to the start of stage one. Be prepared for a BIG climb to start. NO SHUTTLES.

     – All racers must be at the start of stage one prior to 12:00pm. It is your responsibility to understand the distance to the start of stage one and to be there on time. A race official will clear the course at 12:00pm. If a racer does not make it to the top by 12:00pm the race official will instruct them to turn around. If you do not make it to the top by 12:00pm you will not race.

5. How long will I have to wait before I start stage one?
     – Minimum of 90 minutes and up to two hours. Be prepared. Bring water. Bring snacks. Bring sunscreen and bug repellant. The top waiting area is a grassy field in the forest. 

6. Can I use a private shuttle?
     – NO.

EventNotes:
A full weekend of food, bikes and camaraderie you won't soon forget.

We've pulled the best bits of local riding into these loops and we can't wait to share them. Panoramic views across the river valley into Vermont, quiet rolling gravel, no shortage of leg-busting climbs, and a good helping of Class VI — the unmaintained old town roads that make this ride what it is. 

Saturday

  • Shakeout ride led by your hosts if enough sign ups
  • Swim in the lake
  • Wood-fired feast at the pavilion
  • Camping on site

Sunday

  • Complimentary breakfast and coffee
  • Four routes to choose from (links below) + a Family Friendly ride
  • A staffed feed stop on every route, stocked with Orchard Hill Breadworks baked goods, water, drink mix, fruit, and maple syrup shots
  • Post-ride pizza and dessert for all riders. Eat up — we're not counting slices.

A note on the elevation numbers: the figures above are what your head unit will record. The Ride with GPS route pages will read several hundred feet lower, because the mapping data smooths out our rollers and there are hundreds of them. Nobody's shorting you.

Navigation

The courses are self-navigated, and there is little to no marking on course. We like arrows, but we share these roads and trails with a wide range of other users, and it's become clear not everyone shares our enthusiasm for them. No arrows beats wrong arrows.

GPS files and cue sheets go out by email two to three days before the event. Ride with a navigation device. Printed cue sheets are available at check-in — take one even if you're sure you won't need it. Batteries die, units freeze, and there are no arrows to fall back on.

What to bring

  • Good, Bad and Ugly: 45 - 50mm tires if you have them. Back in the day we were riding these routes on 38s. Every time we ride them now, on something bigger, we think “How and Why!?!?”
  • Type 1 Fun: rideable on 32mm, but you'll be happier on 38–42mm.
  • This ride is self-supported. Bring what you need for flats and minor repairs, including two tubes.
  • SAG is available on call, but on some sections that means walking a while to find cell reception or a road. Plan accordingly.
  • Pizza is wood-fired with a range of toppings. Gluten-free crusts available.
  • BYOB.
  • More about the venue: www.orchardhillbreadworks.com

Motor vehicles are not restricted on the routes of the Amish Country Bike Tour. Follow all rules of the road. Never cross a yellow line, not even to pass. 

To promote safety and relieve congestion, a staggered police escorted start based on distance is scheduled out of Dover:

7:00 am 100-mile riders
7:30 am 62-mile riders
8:00 am 50-mile riders
8:30 am 25-mile riders

The Pisgah Monster-Cross Challenge is the premiere all-road racing event in the region. Participants are challenged to complete a 69.2 mile course with 8,777’of climbing along scenic gravel and paved roads. The riders will be treated to some of the finest gravel roads in the Pisgah and Nantahala National Forests, which is a one-of-a-kind opportunity in the racing world. Monster-Cross is a dream gravel endurance event where keen race tactics and strategy, along with overall fitness, proper gear selection, and sheer luck are key to success. 

There will be three Rest Areas along the way that will be stocked with water, food (PB&J, fruit, salty snacks, sweet snacks,  bars), first aid, and neutral mechanical support. Racers will be covering a lot of ground on the map, riding through some of the most quintessential Pisgah forest, not without brutal terrain and breathtaking scenery.

The Georgia TT Endurance Challenge for 2027 - Sept 11-12

The 2nd year of Ga TT Event in 2026 was a great success and I am happy to report we will have it again in 2027. This event is 1 of 6 UltraCycling Events (UCE) in the growing Catalog of events on the WUCA calendar.

This event will again be WUCA's 6-hr NA Championship again for 2027

This is a great route to rack up your UltraCycling miles. Ride virtually flat, low traffic roads while you ride the 29 mile loop during the day. The 29-mile route will go from New Ebenezer Retreat Center to the sleepy little town of Clyo and back. With hardly any trucks and low traffic you will enjoy the peace and serenity of South Georgia during the last weeks of summer. For the 24-hour riders, at night there is a 6-mile night loop so you will only be at a max 3 miles from the start-finish at any point. It also loops from the New Ebenezer Retreat Center to a large traffic circle and back to a nice 3-lane wide dead-end for 2 easy turns. 

There will be 100-mile, 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour events complete with gender , 5-year age groups, and all bike type categories. As well as solo, and 2x-8x teams. There is something for everyone!

Bike category rules :

Since this is an ultra-cycling event and not a UCI event, it is much more relaxed:
You can use any bike you like, and yes, you can swap bikes during the event if you want? - as long as it is in the same category (upright, etc) People ride everything from dedicated TT bikes to standard road bikes.
Yes, you wear a Camelback, aero helmet, special socks, and you are welcome to wear headphones for music - although I would personally advise you to use headphone that don't actually go in your ears.
The only real restriction is that if you have something on you or your bike that “fairs you” the rider (like a wind-screen) - then that puts you into a “faired” category - this is for any type of bike. aero helmets, socks are excluded since they are accepted and used globally now. 
Your bike does not need to pass a jig or any specific measurement tests.

RAAM Qualifier: The 24-hour non-drafting will be a RAAM qualifier (RQ). RQ is 400 Miles for men and 370 miles for women (and 60+ men).

Important Dates:

  • Aug 11, 2027 - Last Day to register and order a custom 2026 Sav-TT-Endurance t-shirt, jersey and/or Medallion
  • Sept 10, 2027 (Fri) - 5pm - Final day for online registration
  • Sept 10, 2027 (Fri) - 4pm - 7pm - Packet pickup and onsite registration - RFID pickup

Starting Day Activities/Schedule: Start on Sept 13th - 7:00am

  • 6:45am - All riders meet at start line to go over final announcements

  • Awards will be at the Start/Finish line after each event as soon as the final rider is in and results can be tabulated - usually within 30 minutes.

Main Venue: The hub of the event will be the New Ebenezer Retreat Center. The address is 2887 Ebenezer Rd, Rincon, GA 31326. Drive down Ebenezer road (about 3 miles from the traffic circle) almost to the very end. The large cities of Pooler and Georgia also have many standard hotels that can also meet your needs. Most are within 20-30 minutes of the race site.

Packet Pickup and on-site Registration:

2 weeks before the event I will email you a digital packet - with a link to e-sign your waiver. All you need to do then is pickup your RFID chip and test it, then show up on Sat morning at about 6:30am. To do this - go to the race directors tent set up by the edge of the road in front of the parking lot. The address is 2887 Ebenezer Rd, Rincon, GA 31326
