  • Sat, Sept 11, 2027 - 5:30 - 6:30am - event day packet pickup and onsite registration, and RFID pickup and test

Awards will be given at this location after each event as soon as results can be tabulated - Usually within 30 minutes.

The Events:

There will be 4 primary events at Georgia TT Endurance Challenge: 100 Mile, 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour Challenges.

Each event will have the following categories: gender, 5-yr age-groups, all bike types, non-drafting or drafting, supported or self-supported, solo as well as 2 thru 8 rider teams.

All 6, 12, and 24 hour timed events will follow this format:

  • Ride the 29-mile Ebenezer-Clyo loop until you cannot ride another one before your time expires (or gets dark for 24-hr & 500 mile riders), then

  • Ride the 6-mile loop on Ebenezer Road between the Retreat Center and the traffic circle

The 100-Mile (Century) event will follow this format

  • Ride the 29-mile Ebenezer-Clyo loop 3 times, then

  • Ride the 6-mile loop on Ebenezer Road 2 times - for a total of 102 miles.

Courses:

29-mile loop: The 29-mile loop leaves from the main road in front of New Ebenezer Retreat center, turns right at the traffic circle, then right on Stillwell-Clyo road all the way to Clyo, makes a U-turn right as the road takes a sharp left (There will be a sign and arrows on the road so you know where to turn), and then head back to New Ebenezer by the same route, passes by the start-finish to a small cul-de-sac at the end of Ebenezer road and ¼ mile back to the start/finish line.

  • Strava Course GXP you can view and download to your GPS Unit: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/51451933

  • Video of 29 mile loop: https://youtu.be/jjd5RR1hoeU

6-Mile loop: The 6-mile loop starts at the same start-finish and goes for 3 miles to the traffic circle where you head straight back and passes by the start-finish to a 3-lane wide bulb at the end of Ebenezer road and ¼ mile back to the start.  Just 2 easy turns each 6 miles on perfectly flat and smooth pavement.

  • Strava Course GXP you can view and download to your GPS Unit: https://www.strava.com/routes/3337187575046476868

  • Video of 6 mile loop: https://youtu.be/qvRqMyI8gxI

Event protocol:

All events and riders will start and finish at the entrance to the Timing Tent setup next to the road directly in front of the main building.

All riders will leave together at 7am , letting the drafting riders take the lead.

All 6 & 12-hour riders will ride the 29-mile Ebenezer-Clyo loop continuously; if they cannot complete another loop before their time runs out, then they ride the 6-mile loop until their last lap has gone beyond their time.

All 24-hour riders will ride the 29-mile Ebenezer-Clyo loop until dark, then they switch over to ride the 6-mile loop until their last lap has gone beyond their 24-hour time.

The Century riders will ride 3 loops of the 29-mile course and 2 loops of the 6-mile course for a total of 102 miles.

If you are in any non-drafting category, you must honor the “non-drafting zone”. We have adopted the USA Triathlon (USAT) definition of this ‘zone’: as a “rectangular area seven 7 meters long (23 feet) and two 2 meters wide (6.5 feet) surrounding each bicycle”. This will provide a sufficient non-drafting area around each cyclist.

This event is also aligning with the World Record setting standards within World UltraCycling Association (WUCA). This format allows all riders to ride until the very end of their timed event. No more of “If you can’t make it around the loop before the time expires - you are done”. Everyone will be encouraged and allowed to complete the current lap they are on until their time event expires. Your distance covered during your final partial lap will be prorated based on your final lap time that way you get maximum distance for your event time..

Follow vehicles and crew Info:

29-Mile Course Support rules:

If you are riding in the supported category on the 29-mile you are allowed to have a personal support vehicle on the course to assist you. These are the rules for your crew:

  1. You may not directly follow your rider as that would present a dangerous situation with so many riders on the road. If you are seen doing this, your rider will be immediately disqualified from the event and required to stop.
  2. You may be on the course and stop at a pre-arranged location to hand off food or drink to your rider or offer any other type of assistance they need. Clyo is a great place for this and is 15-miles away.
  3. Your rider may call you if they need mechanical aid and you may drive to, and stop anywhere on the course to offer mechanical aid as long as it is done off the road.
  4. Handoffs from the support vehicle while it is moving are not allowed. If you are seen doing this, your rider will be immediately disqualified from the event and required to stop. 

During the 29-mile loop, supported riders may have their crew set-up anywhere along the route as long as they are completely off the road and not on private property.

6.0 Mile Loop Support rules:

Each rider is allowed to set up a single “support area” along Ebenezer Road. (You cannot park your cars along the edge of the road in front of Jerusalem church or New Ebenezer Retreat Center). It is a very small walk from the New Ebenezer parking lot to set up whatever you want along the road. It can be a small event tent with chairs, cooler, etc. It must be totally off the road. Since home base is at the retreat center it is highly encouraged that you use the area as close to it as possible.

Where to park your vehicle:

  • You may park your vehicle in the New Ebenezer parking area. Campers are allowed to park here too.

There is no lighting or access to electricity in the parking area so 24-hr riders and crew need to make sure to supply whatever you need in this regard. You are allowed to run a low-noise generator if you need to.

If your cyclist has a mechanical issue on either course you are allowed to ride out to them to help them. At that point you have 2 options:

  • Repair or replace their bike and let them continue on, or if that cannot be done

  • Bring them and their bike back to the Retreat Center to see if it can be repaired there. If it can, then you must take them back to the exact spot you picked them up at so they can continue your lap. (If you do this, you must let your Event Director know)

Support crew is permitted to hand-off food and drink to their riders from the roadside while the rider is moving. If the riders need to come to a full stop, they must be off the road so they do not interfere with any other rider.

Riders, when you are riding past all the support areas, ride near the left side of your lane (the center of the road) in this designated area so there is no conflict with those slowing down for handoffs or entering the road from a pit-stop.

Self-Supported Category:

If you ride Self-Supported, this means that you are “totally” self-supported. You should carry with you everything you need to fix most issues that might arise, but especially a flat tire. You cannot have anyone help you in any way in the Self-Supported Category. If you get in a bad way on the course (something you cannot fix yourself) and need to call for help, call your Event Director and he will arrange for a SAG vehicle to assist you (no guarantee on time). At this point you must either abandon and take your mileage at that spot - or try and repair your bike and change to the Supported Category.

Awards and souvenirs:

A Georgia TT Medallion is included in your registration fee. It will be given out during the award ceremony and will have your results printed on the back.

During the online registration, you will have the opportunity to purchase custom t-shirts, Cycling Jerseys, or extra Medallions for yourself and your crew. The deadline to preorder is Sept 1, 2026. There will also be a limited supply of Sav-TT t-shirts, Cycling Jerseys, and Medallions available to purchase during onsite registration and packet picket.

An Awards and Recognition Ceremony will be held after each event. Everyone will be recognized for their achievement and have an opportunity for a photo with their medallion and crew. Special recognition will be provided for top overall place in each category.

Awards and recognition ceremonies will be held individually for each event as soon as the results for each event can be tabulated after completion. Award ceremonies will be held at the Start/Finish line - look for the podium - everyone gets recognized and a photo op.

Misc Info:

Many Thanks to New Ebenezer Retreat Center for opening their doors to our event. Please note that no pets are allowed on New Ebenezer property.

Lastly, we are very fortunate that the New Ebenezer Retreat Center has graciously allowed us to use their neighborhood for our event. PLEASE be considerate of the guest, resident, and all drivers you are sharing the road with. Keep off private property and keep noise to a minimum at all times. Use the time immediately after your event (while you are waiting for the award ceremony) to remove all personal items and all trash from your support area.

EventName: 99 Miles of Bad Road Gravel Race
EventNotes:
99 Miles of Bad Road is a gravel bicycle race starting and ending in Hardy, Arkansas.  Expect every road surface type, with roughly 80% being unpaved.  Don't let the elevation profile fool you - Devices have picked up 100 feet or more of elevation gain per mile. These are relentless rolling hills with an occasional punchy climb or chunky descent.  Everything from mud, dirt, gravel, concrete bridges, clay, crushed limestone, creek rocks, broken pavement, and more.  This route earns it's name.  This is an ‘odd year’ so we will be running the loops counter-clockwise! Make sure you download the ODD YEAR files.

There are TWO aid stations on the 56 miler & THREE on the 99 Route.

Starting in 2027 the 199'ers are officially a ‘no crew/support’ category. You can receive things from Road Angels and strangers.

All finishers will receive a cool memento! Top 3 in each category will receive a unique custom award. We have three route options - 56, 99, and 199 miles. 


Check the website and Facebook regularly for updates! Be sure to read the ‘Racer Info’ tab on our website thoroughly! Check out our website here!

--------------

-All three distances of this race are loop routes that start and end at Loberg Park in Hardy, Arkansas.  Camping is available at the campground next door to the park.  We have nothing to do with that, you'll have to reserve with them here if you wish to camp: https://www.campspot.com/park/hardy-campground-rv-park

-Unless there are tornadoes, large hail, or extreme thunderstorms the day of the race, we will not cancel.  Put your big boy/girl pants on, and ride!

-You are solely responsible for your own safety.

- Despite the risk of people tampering with arrows/flagging, we WILL mark the 56 mile course this year, well enough in advance to prevent timing issues. This does mean that some markers could be moved or taken down by people, so you must make sure you have the right GPX file on your phone, watch, or computer. You are responsible for studying the route maps and navigating.  That's half the fun!

This year, the Bicycle Ride Across Tennessee (BRAT) will have one amazing Basecamp — Paris Landing State Park! Join us September 11–16, 2027, for six days of scenic cycling, outdoor adventures, great food, and time spent with a welcoming cycling community.

Each day, riders will have multiple routes to choose from, with distances ranging from 25 to 100 miles throughout the week. All routes will be supported by Tennessee State Park Rangers and volunteers. Expect fully stocked SAG stops every 15–20 miles with water, Gatorade, fresh fruit, nutritious snacks, restrooms, and friendly faces along the way. Rangers will patrol the routes with their blue lights on to alert motorists of your presence, and our on-site mechanic will be nearby to help when bike troubles arise.

 

A Basecamp with a Little Extra Comfort

BRAT 2027 combines outdoor adventure with the comforts of a luxury lodge. Paris Landing State Park offers an on-site restaurant and bar, plus a swimming pool that all BRAT participants can enjoy during their stay. Whether you’re relaxing after a long ride, catching up with friends over dinner, or unwinding poolside, Basecamp is a place to recharge and enjoy the experience beyond the miles.

Participants have several accommodation options to choose from. Primitive camping in the park’s day-use area near the small shelter is included with BRAT registration. The camping area will have restrooms, portable toilets, water access, and a shower truck.

Prefer a different kind of stay? Participants can reserve lodge rooms, cabins, camping cabins, or RV and tent campsites directly through Paris Landing State Park. Lodge rooms and cabins can be reserved online here. To reserve a camping cabin or an RV or tent site, call the park’s main office at (731) 641-4465 and mention that you are with BRAT.

 

More Than Just a Bike Ride

The adventure doesn’t stop when you get off your bike. Back at Basecamp, you’ll find plenty of ways to enjoy your time at the park and explore the surrounding area. Take part in Ranger-led programs, guided hikes, paddling adventures, painting activities, yoga, or a relaxing massage. Join a daytime excursion to Land Between the Lakes or the Tennessee National Wildlife Refuge, or take advantage of Paris Landing’s self-service paddling kiosk to get out on the water.

In the evenings, gather with fellow riders for live music, complimentary tastings, and time to unwind. Tennessee Brew Works will kick things off with its complimentary beer tasting on Saturday, with additional tastings planned throughout the week. Whether you spend your days riding, exploring, relaxing, or a little of everything, BRAT offers plenty of ways to make the week your own.

 

Good Food, Ready for the Ride

Meals are part of the BRAT experience, with breakfast and dinner served at the lodge restaurant on designated days. Start your morning with breakfast favorites, fresh fruit, coffee, and lighter options. In the evenings, enjoy a variety of hearty meals, from Mexican-inspired favorites to pasta and Mediterranean-style dishes. Vegetarian, vegan, and gluten-free options will also be available.

Meals are included based on the length of your BRAT registration:

  • One-day riders: Breakfast on your ride day.

  • Two-day riders: Two breakfasts and one dinner.

  • Three-day riders: Three breakfasts and two dinners.

  • Full-week riders: Breakfast and dinner Saturday through Wednesday, plus breakfast on Thursday.

Want to join the group for an additional dinner? Extra dinners can be purchased during registration for $45 each, or you’re welcome to dine at the restaurant at the lodge.


Choose Your BRAT Experience

Whether you’re ready for the full adventure or can only join us for part of the week, there’s a registration option for you. Choose the full six-day ride, the first three days, the last three days, the weekend, or a single day! Explore our registration options to find the one that best fits your schedule and riding style.

Bringing someone who doesn’t ride? They’re welcome, too! Our non-rider registration option allows friends and family to enjoy afternoon and evening activities, including meals and daily excursions. Excursions take place during the day while riders are out on the routes, making BRAT a great experience for riders and non-riders alike.

The offer is limited to participants under the age of 23 and entrants are verified by their age. Juniors – cyclists under the age of 18 – are eligible to use the same coupon code.

Check-in & Packet Pick Up:

(Watch for updated Information on these dates and locations the below is from 2025 but will likely be the same) 

Friday from 3:00 PM to 6:30 PM at Ourisman Honda in Bethesda, located at 4800 Bethesda Ave, Bethesda, MD 20814. 

Saturday from 2:00 PM to 6:00 PM at Volvo Cars of Frederick / Audi Frederick located at 6001 Urbana Pike, Frederick, MD 21704.

Sunday from 6:00 AM to 30 minutes prior to start (7:30 for #GFNats riders, 8:00 for Gran Fondo riders) at 500 Fleming Ave, Frederick, MD 21701 (at location of race start)

For Gran Fondo Maryland, in order to speed up packet pickup and reduce congestion, riders may collect packets for up to three additional riders. You must present your ID and a copy of each rider’s photo ID and a statement of permission. A text or email containing a photo of a rider’s ID and their statement will work.

Registration will also be available on Saturday and Sunday.

 

Course Description 

After starting in historic downtown Frederick Maryland, the 87 mile Gran Fondo National Series, Gran Route, will gain over 10,000 feet of elevation through several different state parks, municipal forests, protected watersheds, and the Catoctin Mountain National Park.  Riders will travel northwest out of the city of Frederick before entering the Frederick Municipal Forest where the first timed section will gain over 1270 feet in a 5.6 mile race segment. At the top riders will be able to relax and enjoy the cool mountain forest as the course plummets over the west side of the mountain range.

The second timed section ascends the southern approach to Harp Hill for a punchy up-down-up-down-up lasting for a brief 1.4 miles and 279 feet of vertical gain. For the next 25 miles and 2500 feet of cumulative gain, the route then follows a mix of small and obscure backroads heading north towards the decommissioned military base of Fort Ritchie.

Time Section #3 is a more dynamic segment and certainly cannot be called a timed climb. Section #3 will require riders to use caution and technical skill with several 90° turns including an old bridge crossing and tarp & chip road surface. The section starts on a wide downhill roadway where for the first 4.9 miles riders lose 500 feet of elevation before hitting the last 1k and 300 vertical feet to the finish of section #3 on top of Hornets Nest Road. Time segment #3 known as The Gully of Darius is a total of 5.5 miles -574 /+386 feet.  From here the route heads south and works its way back exploring nooks and crannies in the Catoctin Mountain Range and travels through Catoctin Mountain National Park  for 22 miles and +2250 feet of untimed pedaling. Past riders will be able to take special appreciation as they descend Park Central Road, which was used in the opposite direct as race section #2 in past years.

As Gran Route riders approach mile 71 they need to take in a deep breath, shake out their legs and prepare for the hardest segment of the day, (this segment also counts as a time segment for Medio Route riders). Section #4 is 11.4 miles +1203 feet and will test every rider’s ability! The segment starts by gaining 784 feet over the first 4.6 miles and then continues for a challenging and undulating 6.8 miles on top of the mountain ridge on Gambrill Park Road through Frederick Watershed and into Gambrill State Park. After completing time section #4, riders will have over 1000 feet of elevation on their side as they drop off the mountain range and into the valley towards the finish, but completing the route in not over, there are still some hills that are sure to make riders know they are still alive. Riders will return back into historic downtown Fredrick and be welcome to well deserved festivities at the finish line, complete with great food, beverage, and more fun.

SAMBA BASH Rattling Creek Mountain Bike Festival

September 16 - 19, 2027

THE BASH IS ON FOR OUR 10th ANNIVERSARY!

REGISTRATION by 9/21/26 to receive a $10 savings for your entry fee. 

REGISTRATION FEE INCREASES BY $10 after SEPTEMBER 3.

The BASH at Muckelratz is a rain or shine non-competitive mountain bike weekend in the Weiser State Forest on the Rattling Creek Trail system. SAMBA holds the event to generate funding to pay for the upkeep and expansion of the Rattling Creek IMBA Epic. Be sure to click “SHOW ALL NOTES” and scroll to bottom of page to review all details!

 

 

WE NEED YOUR HELP! SEEKING VOLUNTEERS, RAFFLE DONATIONS, CASH SPONSORS, DEMO BIKES, MOBILE BIKE MECHANICS. Anyone who commits to volunteering during the event will receive a discount code! If interested in helping make this event a success, send an email to events@sambabiker.com. SAMBA Staff, please be sure to check your @samba.com email account for discount code, contact events@sambabiker.com if you did not receive code.

 

Event Details:

  • Rattling Creek is classic Central PA Rock Garden riding. This is not a beginner mountain biker event, but it is not a race either. The trails are challenging but great riding can be had for most ability groups.
  • For a map please visit: Rattling Creek Trail System. It is also recommended that you download the Trailforks Rattling Creek (IMBA Epic) route to your mobile device in advance.
  • Camping is primitive with portable toilets, outdoor shower facilities and no hook-ups. We have very limited electric connectivity if needed for medical devices. The camping is in and around the main field at camp and the roads in and out are not paved.
  • Win raffle items donated by our awesome sponsors (must be 18+ and CASH ONLY $$$)!
  • Quiet hours at the Camp are strictly from 11 PM to 8 AM. This isn't just a rule; it's a township ordinance put in place because of noise complaints from neighbors. Breaking this rule could result in fines or even the permanent closure of The BASH for next year.
  • Please pack out anything you bring in to help keep our costs down!
  • HELMETS and WAIVERS are required on all groups rides due to our insurance regulations.
  • The event is only canceled due to extreme weather so come prepared for whatever we have.

Additional FAQs:

  • Are there beginner rides in Rattling Creek? There really are no true beginner rides. All the trails are technical and have rock gardens, significant elevation changes, and no easy way out except to try and make the ride. There is often no cell service on most of the trails so you still have to make it out pretty far to even get support.
  • Do I need to register in advance? Pre-registration via BikeReg is preferred. Even if you want to wait until Friday or Saturday to register, please use BikeReg. We prefer not to have to deal with cash and having the correct amount of change on hand.
  • Why is there no family rate? Families are welcome to come, but the this event is all about riding the IMBA Epic Rattling Creek Trail System. Dinner on Saturday is included in the price as are the facilities and rental of the campground.
  • What is the Saturday dinner menu? We will be ordering pizzas with various toppings and subs from the local JoJo's.
  • What about breakfast? Free coffee and bagels available (until we run out) from 730-930am in bunkhouse on Fri and Sat morning (self-serve).
  • Where is the schedule of events? A schedule will be available at the SAMBA tent. Schedule is subject to change, so please verify the latest information on event day.
  • Is water available at camp or do I need to bring my own? Yes water is available at the bunkhouse.
  • What if I am arriving late in the evening? Please check-in the next morning at the SAMBA tent. You can park anywhere within Camp Muckelratz.
  • Are dogs allowed? Yes, well-behaved dogs are permitted ON LEASH! Please ensure your dog is not a nuisance and is not aggressive toward other dogs or people. Also, be responsible and pickup after your pet to keep the area clean for everyone.
  • Is camping permitted on Sunday night? We don't rent Camp Muckleratz past Sunday at 1pm, which is when everyone must leave Muckleratz. You may camp in the state forest at the free campsites, you just have to reserve them, see Weiser State Forest website.
  • What if I want to camp but don't plan on participating in SAMBA activites/rides? We ask that you still register and pay for admission to the event since we need to cover the cost of the campground and portable toilets. If you do not wish to pay the event fee, you may camp in the state forest at the free campsites, you just have to reserve them, see Weiser State Forest website.
  • Are generators allowed? No, generators are not allowed.
  • Are ground fires allowed? No, ground fires are not allowed.
  • What is the address of Camp Muckelratz? 801 Deitrich Rd, Halifax, PA 17032. GPS Coordinates: 40.5412856,-76.7773905
  • What is the address for Lykens Glen Park? Glen Park Rd, Lykens, PA 17048 GPS Coordinates: 40.5622509,-76.6990354
  • Where can I learn about future SAMBA Events, Group Rides, and Trail Work Days? Please be sure to follow us on Luma(click SAMBA Rider - Join and also the Follow button) to get updates about future events!
  • Where should I park if I'm coming for Saturday only and not camping overnight? You can park at the entrance to Camp Muckelratz, see picture below. If this parking area is full, you can also park at the Snowmobile Lot White Oak Rd, Halifax, PA 17032 GPS Coordinates: 40.544711, -76.758519.

September 17–18, 2027 | Bozeman, Montana

The Hell of the Bozone and 2027 WUCA North American Gravel Ultra-Distance Championships

Big Sky. Bigger Waffles. Continental Bragging Rights.

Welkom to the third annual Belgian Waffle Ride Montana. The Hell of the Bozone moves to September 17–18, 2027, and this time we’re serving something substantially bigger.

The World UltraCycling Association (WUCA) has selected BWR Montana to host the 2027 WUCA North American Gravel Ultra-Distance Championships, bringing an approximately 200-mile championship race to our gathering in Big Sky Country.

Meet the Brussels Waffle, named for Belgium’s biggest waffle and destined to become our biggest day on the bike. A Flemish portion with Montana proportions. We suggest arriving hungry.

Montana brings its own scale to the BWR experience: broad valley views, rolling ranchlands, gravel climbs and stretches of backcountry terrain that demand your attention. Fast sections invite you to push. Rougher sectors remind you to leave something in reserve. The scenery is generous. The course has other priorities.

We’ll still have the Waffle, Wafer and Wanna rides, giving riders a choice of adventures suited to their ambitions and appetites. The Brussels Waffle adds an ultra-distance championship challenge for those who hear “200 miles” and somehow interpret it as an invitation.

Choose your helping and make a weekend of it with the BWR community. Bring friends, family and that riding partner who keeps saying, “We should do something big next year.” We’ve provided the destination and several interpretations of “big.” Let the negotiations begin.

Register here!

WEEKEND EXPERIENCE

The weekend brings together rider check-in, the Unroad Expo, riding and the post-ride gathering. Meet the brands, catch up with your people, eat waffles and leave enough time for the stories afterward.

Whether your day ends with a championship jersey or the satisfaction of finishing something you weren’t entirely sure you could, we’ll be there to celebrate it—with waffles, Belgian ale and people who understand why you would.

The detailed 2027 program, venue and start times will be announced on the event page.

THE BRUSSELS WAFFLE: WUCA NORTH AMERICAN CHAMPIONSHIPS

The Brussels Waffle will ask riders to manage their effort, equipment, fueling and the occasional negotiation with themselves over approximately 200 miles of Montana Unroad.

Expect a championship challenge that rewards strength, skill, strategy and the good sense to eat before you become convinced that everyone around you is the problem.

For perspective, the 2026 Montana Waffle covered 106 miles with approximately 7,500 feet of climbing. This next helping deserves some preparation, perhaps beginning with a long and affectionate relationship with your saddle.

Final 2027 routes, elevation profiles, feed zones and championship requirements will be announced as course development is completed.

A JERSEY WORTH THE JOURNEY

WUCA’s championship program recognizes overall champions and age-group winners, giving riders across generations an opportunity to compete for continental honors.

North American championship titles and custom WUCA champion jerseys will be awarded to the overall male and female Brussels Waffle winners, as well as the male and female winners in each designated age group:

  • Under 18

  • 18–49

  • 50–59

  • 60–69

  • 70–74

  • 75–79

  • 80+

That means opportunities to return home with a continental title, a champion’s jersey and enough well-earned bragging rights to sustain several subsequent group rides. We trust you’ll exercise appropriate restraint, although we certainly wouldn’t.

Final age-group eligibility, minimum-age requirements for the Brussels Waffle, membership requirements and award details will be confirmed in the official championship rules.

Explore WUCA’s wider world of championships, records and ultra-distance challenges at ultracycling.com.

COURSE DISTANCES AND REFERENCE

The Brussels Waffle is the new approximately 200-mile championship distance for 2027. The Waffle, Wafer and Wanna figures below are provided as 2026 course references, not final 2027 specifications.

Waffle, Wafer and Wanna figures reflect the final 2026 Montana Race Bijbel. Final 2027 routes, elevation profiles, feed zones and venue will be announced separately.

SERIES STATUS

The 2027 Quad-Tripel Crown calendar and competition format are still being finalized. Participating events, scoring and the number of results required will be announced separately. Utah will not be part of the Crown series because it will operate as a standalone UCI Gravel World Series qualifier.

The Brussels Waffle will serve as the 2027 WUCA North American Gravel Ultra-Distance Championships. Its championship requirements and awards will be detailed in the official rules.

THIRD ANNUAL BWR MONTANA RIDER INFORMATION

RIDER PERKS

The BWR rider offering includes the following. Final distance-specific inclusions, category details and partner offers will appear in registration and the Race Bijbel.

  • BWR musette bag from Neversecond with race-day essentials and sponsor swag

  • BWR branded memento or BWR Bucks for use with participating partners

  • Race number and RFID timing tag for the official finishing time

  • Pre- and post-ride waffles, coffee and beverages

  • Stocked feed zones with hydration and nutrition, including Neversecond

  • Marked courses, traffic control at designated locations and on-course support

  • Post-ride beer and the BWR community celebration

  • Finisher’s trophy beer, with the offering determined by distance and event

  • Unroad Expo access and opportunities to meet cycling brands and partners

  • Bragging rights and more than enough material for the next group ride

  • Podium recognition for the top three in each Waffle and Wafer age category and the top five overall, subject to final 2027 category rules

  • WUCA North American championship titles and custom champion jerseys for designated Brussels Waffle winners, as outlined above and subject to the official championship rules

Official BWR t-shirts, apparel and branded gear will be available through registration and the BWR merchandise area at the expo.

BWR SPONSORS

We are grateful to the partners who help bring the Unroad to life: Bozeman Health, Bozeman Area Chamber, Gallatin Valley TBID, Neversecond, Capriroso, ALMSTHRE, The Lost Abbey, Athletic Brewing Co., Van Rysel Bikes, Unwaffle, UNDERBUDR, FORMULA 100, Bolt and Birdworx.

TRAINING AND NUTRITION

Build your fueling plan before race day with  Neversecond. Whether you’re preparing for the Wanna or committing to the Brussels Waffle, practice your nutrition during training and arrive with a plan your stomach has already approved.

Partner products and any event offers will be shared through the official BWR channels. Additional Brussels Waffle preparation and support information will be published with the championship details.

YOUR PLACE AT THE TABLE

After more than 40 BWR events, we still love watching a peculiar idea become somebody’s unforgettable day on the bike. Hosting the  2027 WUCA North American Gravel Ultra-Distance Championships gives us another reason to gather in Montana and a substantial new adventure to share.

The Brussels Waffle may be the biggest serving, but every distance comes with the ingredients that brought us here: demanding terrain, beautiful surroundings, good people and a happy disrespect for the usual.

Registration for BWR Montana is open. Join us in Bozeman, September 17–18, 2027, and choose your helping.

Find BWR Montana event details and registration here.

CONNECT WITH US

Strava: Belgian Waffle Ride Club

Instagram: @belgianwaffleride

Facebook: Belgian Waffle Ride

YouTube: Unroad UNLTD

EVENT REFUND POLICY

If event insurance was purchased, you may be eligible for a full refund with a valid claim through the insurance provider, Allianz.

  • Full credit up until three months before the event date.

  • 50% credit up until one month before the event date.

  • 25% credit up until one week before the event date.

All credits expire at the end of the 2027 BWR event season.

Gravel Long Course: 

  • Total Distance  64 miles. https://ridewithgps.com/routes/48374062
  • Event Start | 9 AM MDT | Start and end is 511 Glen Street, Wall, SD.
  • Course Estimated Ride Time  4 - 7 hours

If you enjoy the quiet rush of open roads and endless skies, the long course is for you. Starting and ending in Wall, it saves the best views for last. Self-serve aid stations offer water and snacks, with maps and directions guiding riders across gravel, mixed surfaces, and two-track roads through ranch land and open fields. The heart of the route winds past stunning formations in and around Badlands National Park. Wet weather may affect conditions, and alternate routes may be provided. This course operates under permit with the USFS and Badlands National Park.

Note: This is gravel/single track/pavement. Appropriate tires (ie tubeless) are critical to being able to enjoy and complete your ride. 

Cell phone service is poor to fair throughout the course.

 

Gravel Short Course: 

  • Total Distance 35 miles. https://ridewithgps.com/routes/48282476
  • Event Start | 9 AM MDT | Start and end is 511 Glen Street, Wall, SD.
  • Course Estimated Ride Time is 2-4 hours

 This 35-mile route, half pavement and half gravel/dirt, is a perfect introduction to riding off the paved path. The first half is paved, while the second follows dirt two-track below the Badlands Wall, offering beauty and solitude. The course has a few short technical sections. Wet weather may affect conditions, and alternate routes may be provided. This course operates under permit with the USFS and Badlands National Park.

Note: This is gravel/single track/pavement. Appropriate (ie tubeless) tires are critical to being able to enjoy and complete your ride.

Cell phone service is good to fair throughout the course.

 

Pavement Full Forty:  

  • Total distance 38 miles. https://ridewithgps.com/routes/48227153
  • Event Start | 10 AM MDT | Start is 511 Glen Street, Wall, SD and end at Badlands Trading Post & Gas Station, Exit 131 of I90 (shuttle recommended for this course)
  • Course Estimated Ride Time 2.5 -6 hours 

The rugged heart of the Badlands is Hwy 240. Cycling the entirety of Hwy 240 is definitely a challenging ride due to descending and climbing the Badlands Wall several times. Aid stations and restrooms on the course will provide you comfort and ease for your journey. Cell phone coverage is fair to good throughout the course.  

 

Pavement Thirty Something:  

  • Total distance 31 miles. https://ridewithgps.com/routes/48227117
  • Event Start | 10 AM MDT | Start in 511 Glen Street, Wall, SD and end at the Ben Reifel Visitor Center in Badlands National Park. (Shuttle recommended for this course)

 If this is a first organized ride for you, this course is a perfect option for conquering your “fear of distance”.  Aid Stations and restrooms available on this course.

The 2026 Mid Atlantic Super Series consists of 3 separate individual and team competitions in 3 separate forms of mountain bike racing - Cross Country, Endurance and Enduro series.  This is for Series Registration only and does not include any race registrations. Registering for the series is for series points, team points and end-of-season awards and winners jerseys. 

E-Bikes - Some races do have an e-bike non-MASS class. For these races an e-bike is only permitted in the e-bike class. For races without an e-bike class e-bikes are not permitted.

2026 MASS race schedule can be found by clicking HERE to go to the MASS website

Important note - Your Racing Age is determined by your age on December 31st of the current year.  To explain –  for classes like U19 (Under 19) the racer CANNOT turn 19 in the current race year.  Same for U15 (Under 15), the racer CANNOT turn 15 in the current year. Parents - please take note of this when registering your juniors for the races.

Please take a minute to read the Series Race Rules

The MASS website contains the important details about how we run the series. Topics such as the Series Guidelines, General Rules, Upgrade Rules and XC Payouts can be found at

masuperseries.com

MASS registered racers are competing for end-of-season champions jerseys and individual and team awards in the XC and Endurance races. In order to be entered into the MASS series competitions participants must register for the series here and be assigned a series plate number.  Series Registration is a requirement for the series and we will continue to use permanent series number plates with timing chips in them for XC and multi-lap Endurance races.

IMPORTANT - You must register yourself for the series and each race using YOUR BikeReg profile. We cannot have team directors register their team riders all at once because that will cause a major scoring problem. This is because when you create your BikeReg profile there is a unique Racer ID number associated with you and your profile. You do not see this number but it is downloaded for series registration and for each race registration and it is what allows the scoring system to recognize you and assign you your series plate for each race as well as score you properly when race results are imported into our scoring system. One comment for parents that register themselves as well as their children. This can be done, there is a way to have multiple racers in your BikeReg profile. Contact tech support at BikeReg for details. When you register for each race on BikeReg make sure you use your BikeReg profile and do not register as a “guest” or you will not be assigned your series plate and that will cause all kinds of problems.

Series Registration is not required to participate in any MASS races. This registration DOES NOT register you for any of the races. This registration DOES register you for the MASS series of competions - XC, Endurance & Enduro

Series plate. As is the past this is the basis for all scoring for most races (all XC races). If you do not race with your series plate you will not be scored properly at the race and you will not be scored properly for the series. Do not forget your series plate. If you do forget it or lose it you must let us know BEFORE you race with a non-series plate or you will not be scored for the series. Some Endurance and Enduro races will not use series plates.

Team Topics. The only way to earn series points for your team is to be registered for the series and have your team director add you to your team when they do their team registration. Team registration will be done by team directors requesting an access code to be able to login to the MASS Team Registration site and assign team members. It is that registration process that ties you to the team scoring. We do recommend you include your team name in your BikeReg profile so that team name shows up in your results on-line but that team name has nothing to do with getting the points for your team. If you register for a race at the race your team name will not be entered into the timing system because there is not enough time to do that. That means your team name will not show in the on-line results. You will however still earn your team points as long as you raced with your series plate. Check the MASS website for the latest information. 

Most MASS races do not require a USAC license for any classes. Check the race-specific BikeReg page.

   
This MASS series registration is separate from individual race registration.  Any questions please contact support@masuperseries.com.  Visit www.masuperseries.com for more information.  There are no refunds for any reason.

The Pisgah 111 is the quintessential crusher of a cross-country endurance MTB race. Racers follow a 65.1 mile course with 10,200' feet of climbing along the most iconic trails and gravel roads known in Pisgah National Forest. Just peek at the course map and list of trails and you’ll immediately get chills just thinking about the epic scenery and terrain you’ll encounter.

There will be FOUR rest areas (at three locations) for the Pisgah 111  that will be stocked with water, food (PB&J, fruit, salty snacks, sweet snacks,  bars), first aid, and neutral mechanical support. Riders may send drop bags to each rest area. Be sure to read the information below, too. 

The Pisgah 555 will test the strength and endurance of racers by challenging them to complete a 39.7 mile course with 7325' of climbing and is nearly 100% Pisgah single-track. The course traverses some of the great Pisgah classics: Black Mountain, Turkey Pen Gap, Laurel Mountain, and Pilot Rock.

The Pisgah 555 is open to cyclists AND runners.
There will be THREE rest areas for the Pisgah 555 that will be stocked with water, food (PB&J, fruit, salty snacks, sweet snacks, bars), and first aid. Racers may send drop bags to each Rest Area.

The Gravel Roll is pleased to be returning to Opelika, Alabama for our fourth Opelika Okey Dokey for a full weekend in 2027. We will have Friday Night activities, Saturday Race and Saturday night Gravel Roll Season Celebration. In addition we will have a Sunday Funday Bonus Ride for anyone who sticks around.

We will be updating our courses for 2027. We'll still look to keep around the same distances (between 25-35, 60-70, and 90-100) but we want to freshen the landscape up and put a fresh twist on the roads we've been riding the last few years!

Opelika means "Big Swamp" in the Creek language, and you'll ride past dozens of creeks and over bridges seemingly lost to time and space. But don't worry, there's none of the loose stuff here, just hard red dirt interspersed with a sprinkling of gravel across miles and miles of twisting and rolling terrain.

You'll ride through endless timberland and spooky hollows and be rewarded with occasional views of the Fall Line as it stretches across the landscape. Look closely and you may even discover another Appalachiosaurus hiding in plain sight in the road berms.

If you are looking to put some finishing touches on your Unbound training this is the perfect course. While Unbound will lack the curving roads, the short and recurring undulations of the Okey Dokey mimic much of what you will experience in Kansas, of course, we always promise you trees!

Stay posted for more details once we get our early date announcements for the full series launched.

Fly to Pie is run on largely dirt roads through "the gut" of the Northeast Kingdom of Vermont,  26.2, 17. 13.5 and 6.2 mile options.  We schedule it during our Fall Foliage Season.  It is a running and a biking event.  We start at the Airport in Coventry and end at Parker Pie in West Glover with all the pizza you can eat and with a cash bar with Hill Farmstead bear on tap.  The primary biker route is 26.2 miles 

Marathoner bikers start at the airport at 11:00 am

13.5 mile family challengers start at the airport at 11:00 am

We offer a special Family Challenge for parents and their kids biking on our 13,5 mile course.  $75 group price for parents and kids in groups of up to four riders.

Jay Peak provides shuttle busses from Parker Pie back to the Airport.  Some have said it's one of the best parts of the day.

We offer a 20% Team Discount for teams of five or more using the discount code TEAM2026

We are also offering an Early Bird Special of 50% to anyone registering before January 1, 2025.  EARLYBIRD27

Any one 18 or under can bike for $25 regardless of distance. YOUTH27

The 41st anniversary of Autumn in Bonham will celebrate the exciting new growth in Fannin County. With routes from 4 miles to 100 miles on road and gravel, there are options for everyone.  The longer routes take you on a journey within Fannin County with views of Lake Bonham, Bois D’Arc Lake, and the Caddo National Grasslands.  The Vive le Bois d'Arc Family 5K will travel to Powder Creek Park and include some fun stops along the way. Bring the kids and walk, run, or ride this historic scavenger hunt route! The Finish Line Festival will feature vendors, entertainment, options for dining, Rider Recovery and changing areas.  

 

Paved Road Rally routes: 4 miles, 30 miles, 40 miles, 65 miles, and 100 miles

Gravel Rally routes: 47 miles, and 67 miles

Ride with GPS links posted below.

 

Registration and Early Check-In: Friday October 1st, 2027 from 4:00pm - 8:00pm at Neighbors Place Winery, 205 W. 3rd St. Bonham, TX 75418. https://npwinery.com/

 

Event Day Check-In: Saturday October 2nd, 2027 from 6:00am - 7:30am at the Floyd Community Center, 1100 W. 5th St. Bonham, TX 75418. Come hungry! The youth from 7th & Main Church will be serving a $5 pancake breakfast before the ride, with coffee sponsored by Scooter's Coffee. Other local breakfast options are available and featured in the Official Event Guide participants will receive at check-in.

Post-Ride Lunch: After crossing the finish line, registered riders are invited to enjoy a FREE lunch sponsored by Credit Union of Texas and Texas Farm Bureau Insurance. When redeeming your lunch, be sure to vote for your favorite rest stop of the day!

Stick around after your ride and enjoy the Finish Line Festival, featuring vendors, entertainment, Rider Recovery, changing areas, and plenty of food and fun throughout the afternoon, and live music from 4-6pm!

 

Coming in from out of town? Make a weekend of it! Local lodging is available here:
https://bonhamchamber.com/places.../lodging-rv-parks-airbnb/

 

Registration does NOT include t-shirt. Shirts are available for purchase. Orders close Friday September 17, 2027.

Registration fees are non-refundable.

 

Rest stops are approximately every 10 miles and will furnish snacks, Electrolytes, and water.  CPSC approved helmets are required. It is important to start behind the Official Start Line. Starting early or elsewhere along the route is unsafe. No pets or headphones.

EventName: Lazy Llama Gravel Ride, Mounds Oklahoma
EventNotes:
Lazy Llama gravel ride is meant for fun, enjoying friends and riding bicycles. 

Thank you to our sponsors for helping make this a great event: 

 

 

We support Team Suicide Prevention. Each entry fee, we will give back dollars to help "save a life".

Suicide is one of the forgotten illnesses. We all have been touched by someone taking their own life.
We are all affected one way or another. Join us in helping “save a life.”

 

We have great sponsors and a great course. Plus for the faster riders, we have a “Shared Cash Pot”, Simply put, you finish the 110  mile route in 5 hours 30 minutes, you will share in the cash of $2,000. If no one achieves time in 2027, Bixby Bicycles will add $1,000 in 2028

We will offer tent camping and small RV camping on site at Mounds Park.  We will have Prota Johns, not electric or water hook up.

Pancakes and bacon for breakfast and burgers for lunch.

 

When: Saturday, Oct 9th, 2027

Breakfast 6:30 AM - FREE Pancakes and bacon

Start time: 7:00 AM - 110 mile cash riders 

Start Time: 8:00 AM - 12 - 25 - 50 Mile routes

Where: Alt 75 and 14th street, Mounds OK

Finish line:  Enjoy a few hot dogs, cold drinks and lots of friends to enjoy our sport. 

Tent camping available: Porta pots bathroom will be available, no electric or running water / located in Mounds at 14th street on west side of the road next to the park or in the park. It is approved by Mounds City

Contact: Bixby Bicycles - bixbybicycles@gmail.com or 9189436700 

Entry Fees:

  • Standard Entry ($20): Covers 10, 25, 50
  • Price will increase to $30 dollars on Monday October 1st
  • Cash Pot Entry ($60): Includes race entry and eligibility for the "Cash Pot" (100-mile route only).
    • Price will increase to $70 dollars on Monday October 1st
  • No refunds, no transfer to next year. If you pay and don't ride, thank you for the donation
  • Self-Sufficiency: Routes are unmarked. Routes will be on Strava only.  Riders must carry their own water and nutrition. We will carry your water to the rest stop.
    • 12-mile route: No rest stop.
    • 25-mile route: No rest stop.
    • 50-mile route: One water stop at the halfway point and at the end. In Beggs OK at the South East corner of HWY 75 Alt and HWY 16.
    • 100-mile route cash riders: One water stop at the halfway point and at the end. In Beggs OK at the South East corner of HWY 75 Alt and HWY 16 and at the corner of HWY75 and 14th street, starting your second lap.
  • Course Cut-off: The finish line closes at 1:00 PM. Please plan your pace accordingly.
  • Safety: Helmets are mandatory at all times. Use of earbuds is strictly prohibited.
  • E bikes: E bikes are welcomed, but can not participate in the “cash pot”, E bikes can not assist in helping riders in the “cash pot”. Any assistance from E bikes will be automatically disqualified.
  • Officials will be on course looking for E bike drafting.

Routes

  • 12-mile route: https://www.strava.com/routes/3525639206447668974
  • 25-mile route: Strava Link https://www.strava.com/routes/3496236093824792610
  • 50-mile route: Strava Link https://www.strava.com/routes/3495938056873598010
  • 100-mile "Cash" route: https://www.strava.com/routes/3543335899147402124
    • The 108 mile route is only for Shared Cash riders.

"Cash" 100-Mile Route Details

Bixby Bicycles has established a $2,000 Shared Cash Pot 2026.

Eligibility & Payout:

  • Requirement: Riders must complete the designated 108-mile "Cash" route with time less than 5 hours 30 minutes. You can work together or bring a team.
  • Verification: You must provide proof of your ride via Strava/Garmin data. All data must match the promoter's official route exactly; simply matching the distance is not sufficient. You must ride the route on Strava / Garmin. If you go off course and you don't back track to the original course, you will not be eligible for any “shared cash”, even if you went further than the planned route.
  • Validation: A neutral party will verify all routes and times. Payout will be the following week based upon the verification of time and maps.
  • Payout: If multiple riders meet the criteria, the $1,000 pot will be shared equally among them. Note: A single rider is capped at a maximum payout of 50% of available cash.
  • Rollover: If no riders meet the criteria, the $1,000 pot will roll over to 2027, with an additional $1,000 added, creating a $2,000 pot for 2027. Bixby Bicycles will add $1000 dollars each year up to $5000 dollars 
  • Traffic Laws: Obey all traffic laws. It is your responsibility to stop, go, yield or other. 
  • No e bikes or help from E bikes or out side source other than riders in the 108 mile category

2027 WSBA Membership is $35 through the end of  2026, and $45 thereafter!

If you are an OBRA member in good standing, you can purchase an annual WSBA membership for the great price of $25! Please email ckenlan@obra.org  to access the discount. We are trying to make racing more affordable and accessible. 

Your membership dollars support competitive cycling in the Pacific Northwest with funds going to our race equipment, racer clinics, grants as well as support to encourage new and returning races…and a host of other opportunities. Every single dollar from your membership goes back into building and supporting you, the racers…and the backbone, our great promoters! We cannot do this without you. It takes every one of us.

Dear gravel riders, soul surfers & anyone who uses the bike to  escape time... 

It's Heidi Rentz & Zander Ault here...

We are co-creators of The Spirit World 100 & The Cyclist's Menu, gravel cyclists, chefs & party animals. We're so freaking excited to see you in Patagonia, Arizona for a gravel road race that has inspired every aspect of our lives.

The Arizona Borderlands are known for it's rugged, stunning landscapes & views that you'd never guess existed. You have to see it with your own eyes! Throughout the Spirit World 30, 50, 80, & 100 mile courses - you'll climb up + down & around elevations that range between 4,000 - 6,000 feet above sea level. The San Rafael Valleys demanding terrain asks that you keep your head up at all times. It will be bumpy, winds will always be changing their minds, descents will leave you speechless, and climbs will guide you farther into the Spirit World.

Don't hesitate to reach out with thoughts/questions/ideas... any time. We can't wait to ride bikes and eat food with you this November!

Why does it cost $255 for the 30, 50, 80, & 100 mile race? ??

This special event is capped at only 250 riders & we intend to keep it this small. It's our biggest goal to make it feel like an intimate gathering for 4 days of goodness.

We care deeply about inviting you to experience something you haven't experienced before. 

You won't be disappointed :)

Teeth to the wind,

H & Z

EventName: Hilton Head Cycling Robson Forensic Club/Team 2027
EventNotes:
Hilton Head Cycling/Robson Forensic Cycling Team

Hilton Head Cycling/Robson Forensic Cycling Team (HHC/RF) is a sponsored club licensed by USA Cycling, the national governing body for the sport of cycling in the United States of America.  Founded in 2010, team HHC/RF combined the talents of competitive cyclists from the local Hilton Head/South Carolina Low Country and Savannah areas with additional elite athletes from North Carolina, Pennsylvania, New Mexico and Florida to produce a competitive regional cycling team. Our mission is to promote the sport of cycling and provide quality training and racing environment for accomplished and promising athletes of all ages in the Low Country area, fostering national or international amateur cycling sports competition and supporting development of amateur cycling athletes for that national or international competition, and to promote cycling safety and awareness.

Membership:

Team members range from promising high school age junior riders through accomplished Masters' riders in various age group. Members in all age groups and USA Cycling (USAC) categories have to their credit podium placements at State, Regional and National events.

Competition:

In past seasons, team members have competed in local, region, nation and international events. The 2024 schedule will again include season-long Southeastern and Mid-Atlantic region competitions including our own Rumble @ Roebling weekend event. The race calendar will target State, Regional events and for a select few National Championships and International Competition including World Championships.

Uniforms & Sponsorship:

HHC/RF uniforms have attracted enviable recognition nationally. ...  Upon joining as a club member or a race team member you will be given access to our HHC Pactimo Team Store. Once registered with HHC as a team member and obtaining a USA Cycling race license, please link your license to the Hilton Head Cycling Club at USACycling.org We strongly recommend club riders join the USAC Ride Plus Membership for its insurance and partnership benefits.

Community Cycling & Charitable Support:

Membership has participated in various charitable and community events in support of for example Livestrong/Tour de Shunk, Boys & Girls Club Pedal-4-Kids, bicycle safety training, Savannah Bicycle Campaign, organized developmental/training rides, etc. In addition to these, the team promotes a USAC sanctioned race weekend near Savannah GA.

News articles, press releases and published results with sponsor credit provide market exposure.  Team web site with sponsor name, logo, credit and links to the sponsor designated sites HHC Team Page The team Face Book page is HHC Facebook.
